title.zh: 卷九十五 志第七十一 刑法三
title.raw: 卷九十五 志第七十一 刑法三 Volume 95 Treatises 71: Punishment and Law 3

sentences.zh: 刑法有創之自明，不衷古制者，廷杖、東西廠、錦衣衛、鎮撫司獄是已。

translations.literal: Among punishments and laws that were innovations of the Ming and did not conform to ancient regulations, court beatings, the Eastern and Western Depots, the Embroidered Guard, and the prisons of the Pacification Office are examples.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming introduced several punishments and legal practices that broke with ancient precedent—among them court beatings, the Eastern and Western Depots, the Embroidered Guard, and the Pacification Office prisons.

sentences.zh: 是數者，殺人至慘，而不麗於法。

translations.literal: These several measures killed people in the most cruel fashion and did not fit within the law.
translations.idiomatic: Each of these institutions killed with extraordinary cruelty and operated outside the bounds of formal law.

sentences.zh: 踵而行之，至末造而極。

translations.literal: They were followed in succession until in the dynasty's final years they reached their extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Successive rulers kept them in use until, in the dynasty's closing decades, they reached their worst excess.

sentences.zh: 舉朝野命，一聽之武夫、宦豎之手，良可歎也。

translations.literal: The lives of the entire court and realm were left entirely in the hands of military brutes and eunuch minions — truly lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike entrusted their fate to military thugs and eunuch henchmen—a state of affairs that can only inspire sorrow.

sentences.zh: 太祖常與侍臣論待大臣禮。

translations.literal: The Founder often discussed with his attending officials the proper etiquette for treating great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor often discussed with his close advisers how great ministers ought to be treated.

sentences.zh: 太史令劉基曰：「古者公卿有罪，盤水加劍，詣請室自裁，未嘗輕折辱之，所以存大臣之體。」

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Liu Ji said: "In antiquity when dukes and ministers were guilty, they were given a basin of water and a sword and went to the execution chamber to take their own lives; they were never lightly humiliated — this was to preserve the dignity of great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Liu Ji said, "In antiquity, when a duke or minister was guilty, he was presented with a basin of water and a sword and went to the execution chamber to take his own life. He was never casually humiliated—that was how the dignity of high office was preserved."

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士詹同因取《大戴禮》及賈誼疏以進，且曰：「古者刑不上大夫。

translations.literal: Attending Reader and Academician Zhan Tong thereupon cited passages from the Da Dai Li and Jia Yi's memorial and presented them, saying: "In antiquity punishment did not extend to great officers.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-Waiting and Academician Zhan Tong then cited the Da Dai Li and Jia Yi's memorial and added, "In antiquity, punishment did not reach men of great office.

sentences.zh: 以勵廉恥也。

translations.literal: This was to encourage integrity and a sense of shame.
translations.idiomatic: The purpose was to encourage integrity and shame.

sentences.zh: 必如是，君臣恩禮始兩盡。」

translations.literal: Only in this way could the grace and ritual between ruler and minister be fully fulfilled on both sides."
translations.idiomatic: Only in this way could the bond of grace and ritual between ruler and minister be fulfilled on both sides."

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，工部尚書王肅坐法當笞，太祖曰：「六卿貴重，不宜以細故辱。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu, Minister of Works Wang Su was guilty by law and should have been caned. The Founder said: "The six ministers are of high dignity and should not be humiliated over a minor matter."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongwu (1373), Minister of Works Wang Su was liable under the law to be caned. The Founder said, "The six ministers hold exalted rank and should not be disgraced over a trifling offense."

sentences.zh: 命以俸贖罪。

translations.literal: He ordered that the offense be redeemed with salary.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that Wang redeem the offense with his salary.

sentences.zh: 後羣臣罣誤，許以俸贖，始此。

translations.literal: Thereafter when officials were implicated in errors, they were permitted to redeem with salary — this practice began here.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when officials were implicated in minor offenses, they were allowed to redeem punishment with salary—this practice began here.

sentences.zh: 然永嘉侯朱亮祖父子皆鞭死，工部尚書薛祥斃杖下，故上書者以大臣當誅不宜加辱為言。

translations.literal: Yet Marquis of Yongjia Zhu Liangzu and his son were both beaten to death, and Minister of Works Xue Xiang died under the rod; therefore memorialists said that great ministers who should be executed ought not to suffer added humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Marquis of Yongjia Zhu Liangzu and his son were both flogged to death, and Minister of Works Xue Xiang died under the beating-sticks; memorialists therefore argued that ministers who merited execution should not also be subjected to humiliation.

sentences.zh: 廷杖之刑，亦自太祖始矣。

translations.literal: The punishment of court beating also began with the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Court beatings, too, began under the Founder.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年，怒御史嚴皚、方鼎、何傑等沈湎酒色，久不朝參，命枷以徇。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande, angered that Censors Yan Ai, Fang Ding, He Jie, and others were sunk in wine and women and had long failed to attend court audience, he ordered them placed in the cangue and paraded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande (1428), enraged that Censors Yan Ai, Fang Ding, He Jie, and others had long neglected court audience in favor of wine and women, the emperor ordered them placed in cangues and paraded as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 自此言官有荷校者。

translations.literal: From this time remonstrating officials were sometimes made to wear the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: From this point on, remonstrating officials were sometimes made to wear the cangue in public.

sentences.zh: 至正統中，王振擅權，尚書劉中敷，侍郎吳璽、陳瑺，祭酒李時勉率受此辱，而殿陛行杖習為故事矣。

translations.literal: By the Zhengtong reign Wang Zhen monopolized power; Ministers Liu Zhongfu, Vice Ministers Wu Xi and Chen Yao, and Libationer Li Shimian all successively suffered this humiliation, and beating on the palace steps became established custom.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhengtong reign (1436–1449), with Wang Zhen wielding unchecked power, Minister Liu Zhongfu, Vice Ministers Wu Xi and Chen Yao, and Libationer Li Shimian were among those who suffered this disgrace, and beatings on the palace steps became routine.

sentences.zh: 成化十五年，汪直誣陷侍郎馬文升、都御史牟俸等，詔責給事御史李俊、王浚輩五十六人容隱，廷杖人二十。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chenghua, Wang Zhi falsely implicated Vice Minister Ma Wensheng, Censor-in-Chief Mou Feng, and others; an edict rebuked fifty-six supervising secretaries and censors including Li Jun and Wang Jun for concealing the matter, and twenty men were beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Chenghua (1479), Wang Zhi framed Vice Minister Ma Wensheng, Censor-in-Chief Mou Feng, and others; an edict rebuked fifty-six supervising secretaries and censors, including Li Jun and Wang Jun, for concealing the affair, and twenty men received court beatings.

sentences.zh: 正德十四年，以諫止南巡，廷杖舒芬、黃鞏等百四十六人，死者十一人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhengde, for remonstrating against the southern tour, one hundred forty-six men including Shu Fen and Huang Gong were beaten at court; eleven died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhengde (1519), for opposing the emperor's southern tour, one hundred forty-six officials including Shu Fen and Huang Gong were beaten at court; eleven died.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，羣臣爭大禮，廷仗豐熙等百三十四人，死者十六人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing, when the officials disputed the Grand Rites, one hundred thirty-four men including Feng Xi were beaten at court; sixteen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing (1524), during the Grand Rites controversy, one hundred thirty-four officials including Feng Xi were beaten at court; sixteen died.

sentences.zh: 中年刑法益峻，雖大臣不免笞辱。

translations.literal: In the middle years of the reign criminal law grew ever harsher, and even great ministers were not spared beating and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle period of his reign, penal practice grew ever harsher, and even senior ministers were not spared caning and public humiliation.

sentences.zh: 宣大總督翟鵬、薊州巡撫朱方以撤防早，宣大總督郭宗皋、大同巡撫陳燿以寇入大同，刑部侍郎彭黯、左都御史屠僑、大理卿沈良才以議丁汝夔獄緩，戎政侍郎蔣應奎、左通政唐國相以子弟冒功，皆逮杖之。

translations.literal: Xuan-Da Governor-General Zhai Peng and Jizhou Grand Coordinator Zhu Fang for withdrawing defenses too early; Xuan-Da Governor-General Guo Zonggao and Datong Grand Coordinator Chen Yao for the enemy entering Datong; Vice Minister of Justice Peng An, Left Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao, and Chief Justice Shen Liangcai for deliberating too slowly on the Ding Ru'ao case; Vice Minister of Military Affairs Jiang Yingkui and Left Commissioner Tang Guoxiang for their sons and younger brothers falsely claiming merit — all were seized and beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan-Da Governor-General Zhai Peng and Jizhou Grand Coordinator Zhu Fang were beaten for withdrawing defenses too early; Xuan-Da Governor-General Guo Zonggao and Datong Grand Coordinator Chen Yao, for allowing the enemy into Datong; Vice Minister of Justice Peng An, Left Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao, and Chief Justice Shen Liangcai, for moving too slowly on the Ding Ru'ao case; Vice Minister of Military Affairs Jiang Yingkui and Left Commissioner Tang Guoxiang, because their sons had falsely claimed merit—all were seized and beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 方、燿斃於杖下，而黯、僑、良纔等杖畢，趣治事。

translations.literal: Zhu Fang and Chen Yao died under the rods, while Peng An, Tu Qiao, Shen Liangcai, and others, once the beating was finished, were hurried back to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fang and Chen Yao died under the rods; Peng An, Tu Qiao, Shen Liangcai, and others, once the beating ended, were sent straight back to their duties.

sentences.zh: 公卿之辱，前此未有。

translations.literal: Such humiliation of dukes and ministers had never occurred before.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliation of this kind visited upon senior ministers was unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 又因正旦朝賀，怒六科給事中張思靜等，皆朝服予杖，天下莫不駭然。

translations.literal: Again, on the New Year's Day court audience, angered at the six-section supervising secretaries Zhang Sijing and others, he had them beaten in full court dress; all under Heaven were appalled.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, at the New Year's court audience, he grew angry with the six-section supervising secretaries Zhang Sijing and others and had them beaten while still in full court dress; the whole empire was stunned.

sentences.zh: 四十餘年間，杖殺朝士，倍蓰前代。

translations.literal: Over more than forty years, court officials beaten to death were many times those of previous dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than forty years, the number of court officials beaten to death far exceeded that of any previous age.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，以爭張居正奪情，杖吳中行等五人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, for disputing Zhang Juzheng's release from mourning, Wu Zhongxing and four others were beaten.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wanli (1577), for opposing Zhang Juzheng's refusal to leave mourning, Wu Zhongxing and four others were beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 其後盧洪春、孟養浩、王德完輩咸被杖，多者至一百。

translations.literal: Thereafter Lu Hongchun, Meng Yanghao, Wang Dewan, and others were all beaten; in some cases the strokes reached one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Lu Hongchun, Meng Yanghao, Wang Dewan, and others were beaten as well; in some cases the count reached one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 後帝益厭言者，疏多留中，廷杖寢不用。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor grew ever more weary of remonstrators; memorials were often held in the palace, and court beatings gradually fell out of use.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor grew ever more impatient with remonstrators; memorials were often held back in the palace, and court beatings gradually ceased.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，太監王體乾奉赦大審，重笞戚畹李承恩，以悅魏忠賢。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign, eunuch Wang Tigan, conducting the great review under an amnesty, heavily caned imperial kinsman Li Chengen to please Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign (1621–1627), eunuch Wang Tigan, conducting the great amnesty review, heavily caned imperial kinsman Li Chengen to please Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 於是萬燝、吳裕中斃於杖下，臺省力爭不得。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wan Huang and Wu Yuzhong died under the rods; the censorate strove in vain to prevent it.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Huang and Wu Yuzhong died under the rods; the censorate protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 閣臣葉向高言：「數十年不行之敝政，三見於旬日，萬萬不可再行。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao said: "A corrupt practice unused for decades has appeared three times within ten days; it must by no means be revived."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao said, "A corrupt practice abandoned for decades has resurfaced three times in ten days. It must not be allowed to continue."

sentences.zh: 忠賢乃罷廷仗，而以所欲殺者悉下鎮撫司，士大夫益無噍類矣。

translations.literal: Zhongxian then suspended court beatings and sent all whom he wished to kill down to the Pacification Office; the scholar-official class had ever less room to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian then suspended court beatings and sent everyone he wished to destroy to the Pacification Office prison; scholar-officials had ever less chance of survival.

sentences.zh: 南京行杖，始於成化十八年。

translations.literal: Court beatings at Nanjing began in the eighteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Court beatings in Nanjing began in the eighteenth year of Chenghua (1482).

sentences.zh: 南御史李珊等以歲祲請振。

translations.literal: Southern Censor Li Shan and others memorialized for famine relief because of a year of crop failure.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Censor Li Shan and others petitioned for famine relief after a year of crop failure.

sentences.zh: 帝摘其疏中訛字，令錦衣衛詣南京午門前，人杖二十，守備太監監之。

translations.literal: The Emperor picked out errors in their memorial and ordered the Embroidered Guard to go to the Meridian Gate at Nanjing; each man received twenty strokes, supervised by the garrison eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized on errors in their memorial and ordered the Embroidered Guard to the Meridian Gate at Nanjing; each man received twenty strokes under the supervision of the garrison eunuch.

sentences.zh: 至正德間，南御史李熙劾貪吏觸怒劉瑾，矯旨杖三十。

translations.literal: By the Zhengde reign, Southern Censor Li Xi impeached a corrupt official and provoked Liu Jin; a forged edict ordered thirty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhengde reign, Southern Censor Li Xi impeached a corrupt official and provoked Liu Jin, who forged an edict ordering thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 時南京禁衛久不行刑，選卒習數日，乃杖之，幾斃。

translations.literal: At that time the Nanjing guard had long ceased to carry out punishments; selected soldiers practiced for several days before beating him, and he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing guard had long ceased to administer corporal punishment; selected soldiers practiced for several days before beating him, and he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 東廠之設，始於成祖。

translations.literal: The establishment of the Eastern Depot began with Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Depot was established under Chengzu (Yongle).

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛之獄，太祖嘗用之，後已禁止，其復用亦自永樂時。

translations.literal: The prisons of the Embroidered Guard had been used by the Founder but were later forbidden; their reuse also began in the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Guard prisons had been used under the Founder but were later banned; their revival likewise began in the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 廠與衛相倚，故言者並稱廠衛。

translations.literal: The Depot and the Guard relied on each other; therefore speakers referred to them jointly as the Depot and Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Depot and the Guard relied on each other, so commentators spoke of them together as the "Depot and Guard."

sentences.zh: 初，成祖起北平，刺探宮中事，多以建文帝左右為耳目。

translations.literal: At first, when Chengzu rose in Beiping, he spied on affairs within the palace and largely used men from Jianwen's circle as his eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu first rose in Beiping, he spied on palace affairs, relying largely on men from the Jianwen emperor's circle as informants.

sentences.zh: 故即位後專倚宦官，立東廠於東安門北，令嬖暱者提督之，緝訪謀逆妖言大奸惡等，與錦衣衛均權勢，蓋遷都後事也。

translations.literal: Therefore after his accession he relied exclusively on eunuchs, established the Eastern Depot north of Dong'an Gate, and had his favorites supervise it to investigate treason, heterodox speech, and great wickedness; it shared power equally with the Embroidered Guard — this was an affair after the transfer of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession he relied exclusively on eunuchs, established the Eastern Depot north of Dong'an Gate, and placed his favorites in charge to investigate treason, seditious talk, and grave crimes; it shared power equally with the Embroidered Guard—a development of the post-relocation capital.

sentences.zh: 然衛指揮紀綱、門達等大幸，更迭用事，廠權不能如。

translations.literal: Yet Guard commanders Ji Gang, Men Da, and other great favorites held power in turn, and the Depot could not match them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guard commanders such as Ji Gang and Men Da, as imperial favorites, held power in turn, and the Depot could not rival them.

sentences.zh: 至憲宗時，尚銘領東廠，又別設西廠刺事，以汪直督之，所領緹騎倍東廠。

translations.literal: By the time of Xianzong, Shang Ming headed the Eastern Depot; a Western Depot was separately established for intelligence, with Wang Zhi supervising it; the mounted guards under his command were twice those of the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzong, Shang Ming headed the Eastern Depot while a separate Western Depot was set up for intelligence work under Wang Zhi; the mounted guards at his command were twice the Eastern Depot's strength.

sentences.zh: 自京師及天下，旁午偵事，雖王府不免。

translations.literal: From the capital to all the realm, investigations crisscrossed in every direction; even princely establishments were not spared.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital to the provinces, agents crisscrossed the land on surveillance missions; even princely establishments were not spared.

sentences.zh: 直中廢復用，先後凡六年，冤死者相屬，勢遠出衛上。

translations.literal: Zhi was dismissed and restored to use in the middle; altogether for six years wrongful deaths followed one upon another, and his power far exceeded that of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was dismissed and restored mid-career; over six years in all, victims of wrongful death followed one after another, and his power far outstripped the Guard's.

sentences.zh: 會直數出邊監軍，大學士萬安乃言：「太宗建北京，命錦衣官校緝訪，猶恐外官徇情，故設東廠，令內臣提督，行五六十年，事有定規。

translations.literal: As Zhi repeatedly went out to the frontier to supervise troops, Grand Secretary Wan An said: "When Taizong built Beijing, he ordered Embroidered Guard officers to investigate, still fearing that outside officials might show partiality; therefore he established the Eastern Depot and had inner eunuchs supervise it. For fifty or sixty years matters have had fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Zhi repeatedly went to the frontier to supervise troops, Grand Secretary Wan An said, "When Taizong built Beijing, he ordered Embroidered Guard officers to conduct investigations, still fearing that outside officials might show favoritism; hence the Eastern Depot, placed under inner eunuchs. For fifty or sixty years the arrangement has had settled rules.

sentences.zh: 往者妖狐夜出，人心驚惶，感勞聖慮，添設西廠，特命直督緝，用戒不虞，所以權一時之宜，慰安人心也。

translations.literal: Formerly when a demon fox appeared by night the people's hearts were alarmed and the sage's concern was stirred; the Western Depot was added and Zhi was specially ordered to supervise investigations to guard against the unforeseen — this was to weigh temporary expediency and reassure the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When a demon fox was reported abroad at night, the people were alarmed and His Majesty was troubled; the Western Depot was added and Wang Zhi was specially charged with investigations to guard against unforeseen trouble—a temporary expedient meant to reassure the public.

sentences.zh: 向所紛擾，臣不贅言。

translations.literal: The disturbances of the past your servant will not rehearse at length.
translations.idiomatic: I will not rehearse at length the disturbances that followed.

sentences.zh: 今直鎮大同，京城眾口一辭，皆以革去西廠為便。

translations.literal: Now that Zhi is garrisoned at Datong, throughout the capital all voices as one say that abolishing the Western Depot would be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Wang Zhi is garrisoned at Datong, everyone in the capital agrees that abolishing the Western Depot would be best.

sentences.zh: 伏望聖恩特旨革罷，官校悉回原衛，宗社幸甚。」

translations.literal: Your servant humbly hopes that by special imperial grace it may be abolished by edict and all officers and guards returned to their original guard — the altars of state would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that Your Majesty issue a special edict abolishing it and return all officers and guards to their original posts—the altars of state would be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 尚銘專用事，未幾亦黜。

translations.literal: Shang Ming monopolized power but was soon dismissed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Ming monopolized power but was soon dismissed too.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，員外郎張倫請廢東廠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi, Assistant Department Director Zhang Lun requested abolition of the Eastern Depot.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi (1488), Assistant Department Director Zhang Lun petitioned to abolish the Eastern Depot.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no response.

sentences.zh: 然孝宗仁厚，廠衛無敢橫，司廠者羅祥、楊鵬，奉職而已。

translations.literal: Yet Xiaozong was benevolent and generous; the Depot and Guard dared not act arrogantly; those who managed the Depot, Luo Xiang and Yang Peng, merely performed their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiaozong was benevolent and magnanimous; the Depot and Guard dared not throw their weight around; Luo Xiang and Yang Peng, who ran the Depot, merely performed their duties.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，殺東廠太監王嶽，命丘聚代之，又設西廠以命穀大用，皆劉瑾黨也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, Eastern Depot eunuch Wang Yue was killed and Qiu Ju ordered to replace him; the Western Depot was again established with Gu Dayong appointed — all were Liu Jin's faction.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde (1506), Eastern Depot eunuch Wang Yue was killed and Qiu Ju appointed in his place; the Western Depot was re-established under Gu Dayong—all were part of Liu Jin's faction.

sentences.zh: 兩廠爭用事，遣邏卒刺事四方。

translations.literal: The two Depots vied for power and sent patrol guards to spy in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: The two Depots competed for power and sent patrol guards to spy throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 南康吳登顯等戲競渡龍舟，身死家籍。

translations.literal: Wu Dengxian of Nankang and others playfully raced dragon boats; they died and their households were registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dengxian of Nankang and others staged a playful dragon-boat race; they were executed and their households confiscated.

sentences.zh: 遠州僻壤，見鮮衣怒馬作京師語者，轉相避匿。

translations.literal: In remote prefectures and secluded districts, when men in bright clothes on spirited horses speaking the capital dialect were seen, people turned to hide from one another.
translations.idiomatic: In remote prefectures, the sight of men in bright clothes on spirited horses speaking the capital dialect sent people fleeing in every direction.

sentences.zh: 有司聞風，密行賄賂。

translations.literal: Local officials, catching wind of this, secretly offered bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials, catching wind of their approach, secretly offered bribes.

sentences.zh: 於是無賴子乘機為奸，天下皆重足立。

translations.literal: Thereupon ruffians seized the opportunity to do evil; all under Heaven stood as if on overlapping feet.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffians seized the opportunity to commit crimes, and the whole empire lived in fear, afraid to move.

sentences.zh: 而衛使石文義亦瑾私人，廠衛之勢合矣。

translations.literal: Guard commissioner Shi Wenyi was also Jin's private man; the power of Depot and Guard was united.
translations.idiomatic: Guard Commissioner Shi Wenyi was also one of Jin's men; the Depot and Guard were now fully aligned.

sentences.zh: 瑾又改惜薪司外薪廠為辦事廠，榮府舊倉地為內辦事廠，自領之。

translations.literal: Jin further converted the Fuelwood Office's outer fuel depot into an Operations Depot and the old warehouse grounds of the Rong princely establishment into an Inner Operations Depot, which he personally headed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin further converted the Fuelwood Office's outer fuel depot into an Operations Depot and the old warehouse grounds of the Rong princely establishment into an Inner Operations Depot, which he personally supervised.

sentences.zh: 京師謂之內行廠，雖東西廠皆在伺察中，加酷烈焉。

translations.literal: The capital called it the Inner Operations Depot; even the Eastern and Western Depots were kept under surveillance by it, and its cruelty was greater still.
translations.idiomatic: The capital called it the Inner Operations Depot; even the Eastern and Western Depots fell under its surveillance, and its methods were more brutal still.

sentences.zh: 且創例，罪無輕重皆決杖，永遠戍邊，或枷項發遣。

translations.literal: Moreover he created precedents: regardless of the gravity of the offense all were sentenced to beating and perpetual frontier service, or sent off with the cangue about the neck.
translations.idiomatic: He also set new precedents: regardless of the offense's gravity, all offenders were beaten and exiled permanently to the frontier, or sent away wearing the cangue.

sentences.zh: 枷重至百五十斤，不數日輒死。

translations.literal: The cangue weighed as much as one hundred fifty jin; within a few days death followed.
translations.idiomatic: The cangue could weigh as much as one hundred fifty jin; victims died within days.

sentences.zh: 尚寶卿顧璿、副使姚祥、工部郎張瑋、御史王時中輩並不免，瀕死而後謫戍。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Treasuries Gu Xuan, Vice Commissioner Yao Xiang, Ministry of Works Bureau Director Zhang Wei, Censor Wang Shizhong, and others were none spared; on the verge of death they were then banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Treasuries Gu Xuan, Vice Commissioner Yao Xiang, Ministry of Works Bureau Director Zhang Wei, Censor Wang Shizhong, and others were not spared; on the verge of death they were banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 御史柴文顯、汪澄以微罪至淩遲。

translations.literal: Censors Chai Wenxian and Wang Cheng, for minor offenses, suffered dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Chai Wenxian and Wang Cheng were sentenced to dismemberment for minor offenses.

sentences.zh: 官吏軍民非法死者數千。

translations.literal: Officials, soldiers, and commoners who died unlawfully numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of officials, soldiers, and commoners died unlawfully.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，西廠、內行廠俱革，獨東廠如故。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, the Western Depot and Inner Operations Depot were both abolished; only the Eastern Depot remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution, the Western Depot and Inner Operations Depot were abolished; only the Eastern Depot remained.

sentences.zh: 張銳領之，與衛使強尼並以輯事恣羅織。

translations.literal: Zhang Rui headed it; together with Guard commissioner Qiang Ni they used investigations to fabricate cases at will.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rui headed it; together with Guard Commissioner Qiang Ni they used investigations to fabricate cases at will.

sentences.zh: 廠衛之稱由此著也。

translations.literal: The joint designation Depot and Guard became prominent from this time.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the joint term "Depot and Guard" became firmly established.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，東廠芮景賢任千戶陶淳，多所誣陷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, Eastern Depot head Rui Jingxian employed chiliarch Tao Chun, who fabricated many false charges.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing (1523), Eastern Depot head Rui Jingxian employed chiliarch Tao Chun, who fabricated numerous false charges.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉最執奏，謫判廣德州。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Zui remonstrated firmly and was demoted to magistrate of Guangde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Zui remonstrated firmly and was demoted to magistrate of Guangde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 御史黃德用使乘傳往。

translations.literal: Censor Huang Deyong was sent by relay post to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Huang Deyong was dispatched by relay post.

sentences.zh: 會有顏如環者同行，以黃袱裹裝。

translations.literal: It happened that one Yan Ruhuan traveled with them, his baggage wrapped in yellow brocade.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Yan Ruhuan happened to travel with them, his baggage wrapped in yellow brocade.

sentences.zh: 景賢即奏，逮下獄，最等編戍有差。

translations.literal: Jingxian immediately memorialized; they were seized and imprisoned; Zui and the others were assigned to frontier service in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian immediately memorialized; they were arrested and imprisoned; Liu Zui and the others were assigned to frontier service in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉濟言：「最罪不至戍。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Ji said: "Zui's offense did not warrant frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Ji said, "Liu Zui's offense did not warrant banishment to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 且緝執於宦寺之門，鍛煉於武夫之手，裁決於內降之旨，何以示天下？」

translations.literal: Moreover, arrest at the eunuchs' gate, torture in the hands of military brutes, and judgment by secret edicts from within — how can this be shown to all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when arrests are made at eunuchs' gates, confessions forged by military brutes, and verdicts handed down by secret inner edicts—how can such justice be shown to the empire?"

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no response.

sentences.zh: 是時盡罷天下鎮守太監，而大臣狃故事，謂東廠祖宗所設，不可廢，不知非太祖制也。

translations.literal: At this time garrison eunuchs throughout the realm were all dismissed, yet great ministers clung to precedent, saying the Eastern Depot was established by the imperial ancestors and could not be abolished — not knowing it was not the Founder's institution.
translations.idiomatic: At this time garrison eunuchs throughout the realm were dismissed, yet senior ministers clung to precedent, claiming the Eastern Depot had been established by the imperial ancestors and could not be abolished—not realizing it was not the Founder's institution.

sentences.zh: 然世宗馭中官嚴，不敢恣，廠權不及衛使陸炳遠矣。

translations.literal: Yet Shizong controlled inner eunuchs strictly; they dared not act wantonly; Depot power fell far short of Guard commissioner Lu Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shizong kept inner eunuchs on a tight rein; they dared not run wild; Depot power fell far short of Guard Commissioner Lu Bing's.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，馮保以司禮兼廠事，建廠東上北門之北，曰內廠，而以初建者為外廠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Feng Bao, holding the Directorate of Ceremonial while also managing Depot affairs, built a depot north of the North Gate on the upper east side, called the Inner Depot, while the originally established one was termed the Outer Depot.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, Feng Bao, holding the Directorate of Ceremonial while also running Depot affairs, built a new depot north of the upper east gate, called the Inner Depot; the original establishment became the Outer Depot.

sentences.zh: 保與張居正興王大臣獄，欲族高拱，衛使朱希孝力持之，拱得無罪，衛猶不大附廠也。

translations.literal: Bao and Zhang Juzheng raised the Wang Dachen case, wishing to exterminate Gao Gong's clan; Guard commissioner Zhu Xixiao firmly resisted, and Gong escaped guilt; the Guard still did not greatly attach itself to the Depot.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and Zhang Juzheng raised the Wang Dachen case, seeking to exterminate Gao Gong's clan; Guard Commissioner Zhu Xixiao firmly resisted, and Gong was cleared; the Guard still did not align closely with the Depot.

sentences.zh: 中年，礦稅使數出為害，而東廠張誠、孫暹、陳矩皆恬靜。

translations.literal: In the middle years, mining-tax envoys repeatedly went out to do harm, yet Eastern Depot heads Zhang Cheng, Sun Xian, and Chen Ju were all quiet and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle years of his reign, mining-tax envoys repeatedly went out to prey on the provinces, yet Eastern Depot heads Zhang Cheng, Sun Xian, and Chen Ju were all restrained.

sentences.zh: 矩治妖書獄，無株濫，時頗稱之。

translations.literal: Ju handled the demon-book case without indiscriminate implication; at the time he was rather praised.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ju handled the demon-book case without indiscriminate implication and won some praise at the time.

sentences.zh: 會帝亦無意刻核，刑罰用稀，廠衛獄中至生青草。

translations.literal: Moreover the Emperor had no mind for harsh scrutiny; punishments were rarely used; in Depot and Guard prisons grass even grew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no taste for harsh scrutiny; punishments were rarely imposed; grass even grew in the Depot and Guard prisons.

sentences.zh: 及天啟時，魏忠賢以秉筆領廠事，用衛使田爾耕、鎮撫許顯純之徒，專以酷虐鉗中外，而廠衛之毒極矣。

translations.literal: By the Tianqi reign, Wei Zhongxian, holding the brush while heading Depot affairs, employed Guard commissioner Tian Ergeng, Pacification Commissioner Xu Xianchun, and their kind, using cruelty exclusively to clamp down within and without; the poison of Depot and Guard reached its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianqi reign, Wei Zhongxian, holding the brush while running Depot affairs, employed Guard Commissioner Tian Ergeng, Pacification Commissioner Xu Xianchun, and their ilk to terrorize court and country alike; the Depot and Guard reached the height of their cruelty.

sentences.zh: 凡中官掌司禮監印者，其屬稱之曰宗主，而督東廠者曰督主。

translations.literal: Whenever an inner eunuch held the seal of the Directorate of Ceremonial, his subordinates called him Patriarch, while one who supervised the Eastern Depot was called Supervisor Patriarch.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an inner eunuch held the Directorate of Ceremonial seal, his subordinates called him Patriarch; the one who supervised the Eastern Depot was called Supervisor Patriarch.

sentences.zh: 東廠之屬無專官，掌刑千戶一，理刑百戶一，亦謂之貼刑，皆衛官。

translations.literal: The Eastern Depot had no dedicated officials; one chiliarch managed punishments and one centurion handled cases — also called attached punishers — all were Guard officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Depot had no dedicated officials of its own; one chiliarch managed punishments and one centurion handled cases—called "attached punishers"—all drawn from the Guard.

sentences.zh: 其隸役悉取給於衛，最輕黠獧巧者乃撥充之。

translations.literal: Its subordinate servants were all drawn from the Guard; only the most nimble, cunning, and clever were selected for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Its staff were all drawn from the Guard; only the nimblest and most cunning were assigned.

sentences.zh: 役長曰檔頭，帽上銳，衣青素衤旋褶，系小絛，白皮靴，專主伺察。

translations.literal: The head of the servants was called a file-head; his hat had a sharp peak, he wore blue-gray collarless jacket and pleated skirt, a small cord at the waist, and white leather boots, and was devoted exclusively to surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: The head servant was called a "file-head": peaked cap, blue-gray collarless jacket and pleated skirt, small cord at the waist, white leather boots—devoted exclusively to surveillance.

sentences.zh: 其下番子數人為幹事。

translations.literal: Beneath him several "banner-men" served as operatives.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath him several "banner-men" served as operatives.

sentences.zh: 京師亡命，誆財挾仇，視幹事者為窟穴。

translations.literal: Fugitives of the capital, who swindled for money or nursed grudges, regarded the operatives as their lair.
translations.idiomatic: Capital fugitives who swindled for money or nursed grudges treated the operatives as their refuge.

sentences.zh: 得一陰事，由之以密白於檔頭，檔頭視其事大小，先予之金。

translations.literal: When they obtained a secret matter, they reported it confidentially to the file-head through them; the file-head, judging the affair great or small, first gave them money.
translations.idiomatic: When they uncovered a secret, they reported it confidentially to the file-head, who judged the affair's importance and paid them in advance.

sentences.zh: 事曰起數，金曰買起數。

translations.literal: The affair was called raising the count; the money was called buying the count.
translations.idiomatic: The case was called "raising the count"; the payment was called "buying the count."

sentences.zh: 既得事，帥番子至所犯家，左右坐曰打樁。

translations.literal: Once the matter was secured, they led the banner-men to the household of the accused; sitting to left and right was called driving the stake.
translations.idiomatic: Once a case was secured, they led the banner-men to the accused's home and seated themselves on either side—a procedure called "driving the stake."

sentences.zh: 番子即突入執訊之。

translations.literal: The banner-men at once burst in, seized them, and interrogated them.
translations.idiomatic: The banner-men would burst in at once, seize the accused, and interrogate them.

sentences.zh: 無有佐證符牒，賄如數，徑去。

translations.literal: If there were no supporting documents or warrants, and bribes were paid as demanded, they went straight away.
translations.idiomatic: Without supporting documents or warrants, once bribes were paid as demanded, they departed at once.

sentences.zh: 少不如意，扌旁治之，名曰乾醡酒，亦曰搬罾兒，痛楚十倍官刑。

translations.literal: At the slightest dissatisfaction, they beat and tortured them; it was called dry press wine, also called hauling the seine—the agony ten times that of official punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest displeasure they would beat and torture victims—methods called "dry press wine" and "hauling the seine," whose agony exceeded official punishments tenfold.

sentences.zh: 且授意使牽有力者，有力者予多金，即無事。

translations.literal: Moreover they would instruct them to implicate persons of influence; if the influential gave much gold, then there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: They also instructed informants to implicate powerful figures—but if those figures paid a large bribe, the matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 或靳不予，予不足，立聞上，下鎮撫司獄，立死矣。

translations.literal: Or if one stinted and did not give, or gave insufficiently, it was immediately reported above; the person was sent down to the Pacification Office prison—and died at once.
translations.idiomatic: If someone refused to pay or paid too little, word was immediately sent upward; the victim was thrown into the Pacification Office prison and was as good as dead.

sentences.zh: 每月旦，廠役數百人，掣簽庭中，分瞰官府。

translations.literal: On the first of each month, several hundred Depot servants drew lots in the courtyard and were assigned to surveil government offices.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of each month, several hundred Depot operatives drew lots in the courtyard and were dispatched to surveil government offices.

sentences.zh: 其視中府諸處會審大獄、北鎮撫司考訊重犯者曰聽記。

translations.literal: Their observing joint trials of major cases at offices of the central prefecture and the northern Pacification Office's examination and interrogation of serious offenders was called listening records.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance of joint trials of major cases at central prefectural offices and of the northern Pacification Office's interrogation of serious offenders was called "listening records."

sentences.zh: 他官府及各城門訪緝曰坐記。

translations.literal: Surveillance of other government offices and of investigations at the city gates was called sitting records.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance at other government offices and city-gate investigations was called "sitting records."

sentences.zh: 某官行某事，某城門得某奸，胥吏疏白坐記者上之廠曰打事件。

translations.literal: Such-and-such official did such-and-such thing; such-and-such city gate caught such-and-such culprit—a clerk's brief report by the sitting-record keeper submitted to the Depot was called striking events.
translations.idiomatic: When a clerk submitted a sitting-record report to the Depot—"Official X did Y; Gate Z caught culprit W"—it was called a "striking event."

sentences.zh: 至東華門，雖夤夜，投隙中以入，即屏人達至尊。

translations.literal: Reaching the Donghua Gate, even at deep night, they slipped through gaps to enter and, dismissing attendants, reached the Supreme One.
translations.idiomatic: Reports reached the Donghua Gate; even at dead of night the bearers slipped through gaps in the gate, dismissed attendants, and delivered the message directly to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 以故事無大小，天子皆得聞之。

translations.literal: According to precedent, matters great or small—all were heard by the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, matters great and small alike were brought to the emperor's ears.

sentences.zh: 家人米鹽猥事，宮中或傳為笑謔，上下惴惴無不畏打事件者。

translations.literal: Household matters of rice and salt and trivial affairs were sometimes passed about in the palace as jokes—but high and low alike lived in dread, and none did not fear striking events.
translations.idiomatic: Trivial household gossip might circulate in the palace as amusement—but court and realm alike trembled in fear of "striking events."

sentences.zh: 衛之法亦如廠。

translations.literal: The Guard's methods were also like the Depot's.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Guard operated much like the Depot.

sentences.zh: 然須具疏，乃得上聞，以此其勢不及廠遠甚。

translations.literal: Yet they had to submit a formal memorial before it could reach the throne above; for this reason their power fell far short of the Depot's.
translations.idiomatic: The Guard, however, had to submit a formal memorial before reports reached the throne—so its power fell far short of the Depot's.

sentences.zh: 有四人夜飲密室，一人酒酣，謾駡魏忠賢，其三人噤不敢出聲。

translations.literal: Four men were drinking at night in a private room; one, flushed with wine, casually cursed Wei Zhongxian—the other three kept silent and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Four men were drinking in a private room one night. One, drunk, casually cursed Wei Zhongxian; the other three sat frozen in silence.

sentences.zh: 罵未訖，番人攝四人至忠賢所，即磔罵者，而勞三人金。

translations.literal: Before the cursing was finished, banner-men seized all four and brought them to Zhongxian's presence; the curser was at once dismembered, and the three others were pressed for gold.
translations.idiomatic: Before the curses ended, banner-men seized all four and brought them to Zhongxian. The curser was immediately dismembered; the other three were shaken down for gold.

sentences.zh: 三人者魄喪不敢動。

translations.literal: The three men's spirits were shattered; they dared not stir.
translations.idiomatic: The three men's souls were shattered; they did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，忠賢伏誅，而王體乾、王永祚、鄭之惠、李承芳、曹化淳、王德化、王之心、王化民、齊本正等相繼領廠事，告密之風未嘗息也。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, Zhongxian was executed; yet Wang Tiqian, Wang Yongzuo, Zheng Zhihui, Li Chenfang, Cao Huachun, Wang Dehua, Wang Zhixin, Wang Huamin, Qi Benzheng, and others succeeded one another in directing Depot affairs—the wind of secret denunciation never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor came to the throne, Zhongxian was executed—but Wang Tiqian, Wang Yongzuo, Zheng Zhihui, Li Chenfang, Cao Huachun, Wang Dehua, Wang Zhixin, Wang Huamin, Qi Benzheng, and others took the Depot in succession, and the culture of secret denunciation never abated.

sentences.zh: 之心、化淳敘緝奸功，廕弟侄錦衣衛百戶，而德化及東廠理刑吳道正等偵閣臣薛國觀陰事，國觀由此死。

translations.literal: Zhixin and Huachun recorded their merits in apprehending culprits and ennobled younger brothers and nephews as hundred-officers of the Embroidered Guard; meanwhile Dehua and the Eastern Depot magistrate Wu Daozheng and others spied on the private affairs of Grand Secretary Xue Guoguan—and Guoguan died on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin and Huachun recorded their merits in apprehending offenders and secured hereditary posts in the Embroidered Guard for brothers and nephews. Dehua, the Eastern Depot magistrate Wu Daozheng, and others meanwhile spied on Grand Secretary Xue Guoguan's private affairs—leading to Guoguan's death.

sentences.zh: 時衛使慴廠威已久，大抵俯首為所用。

translations.literal: By then the Guard commander had long feared the Depot's power and for the most part bowed his head to be used by it.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Guard commander had long been cowed by the Depot's authority and largely did its bidding.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年，御史楊仁願言：「高皇帝設官，無所謂緝事衙門者。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, Censor Yang Renyuan said: "The High Emperor established offices—there was no such thing as an intelligence bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 15, Censor Yang Renyuan said: "When the dynastic founder established the bureaucracy, there was no such institution as an intelligence bureau.

sentences.zh: 臣下不法，言官直糾之，無陰訐也。

translations.literal: When subordinates broke the law, remonstrating officials directly impeached them—there was no secret denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: When officials broke the law, remonstrating censors impeached them directly—without secret denunciations.

sentences.zh: 後以肅清輦轂，乃建東廠。

translations.literal: Later, to purge the capital region, the Eastern Depot was established.
translations.idiomatic: Later, to purify the capital, the Eastern Depot was established.

sentences.zh: 臣待罪南城，所閱詞訟，多以假番故訴冤。

translations.literal: I serve at fault in the Southern City; in the lawsuits I review, many people plead wrongs on account of impostor banner-men.
translations.idiomatic: In my posting in the Southern City, I see many lawsuits in which people plead injustice because of impostor Depot operatives.

sentences.zh: 夫假稱東廠，害猶如此，況其真乎？

translations.literal: If falsely claiming to be the Eastern Depot the harm is still thus—how much more if it were the real thing?
translations.idiomatic: When even impostors cause such harm, how much worse is the real Depot?

sentences.zh: 此由積重之勢然也。

translations.literal: This results from the accumulated weight of the situation.
translations.idiomatic: This is the consequence of institutional overreach compounded over time.

sentences.zh: 所謂積重之勢者，功令比較事件，番役每懸價以買事件，受買者至誘人為奸盜而賣之，番役不問其從來，誘者分利去矣。

translations.literal: What is meant by accumulated weight is this: through performance quotas comparing striking events, banner-servants each posted prices to buy events; those who sold them went so far as to lure people into being offenders and robbers and then sell them; the banner-servants did not ask how it came about—the lurers took their share of profit and left.
translations.idiomatic: The 'accumulated weight' means this: performance quotas required a quota of striking events, so banner-servants posted prices to buy cases. Sellers went so far as to lure innocents into crime and then sell them as culprits; the banner-servants never asked how the case arose—the entrapers took their cut and departed."

sentences.zh: 挾忿首告，誣以重法，挾者志無不逞矣。

translations.literal: Bearing a grudge, one would first denounce another and falsely charge him under heavy law—the grudge-bearer invariably got his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone nursing a grievance could denounce another and fabricate a capital charge—and invariably get revenge.

sentences.zh: 伏願寬東廠事件，而後東廠之比較可緩，東廠之比較緩，而後番役之買事件與賣事件者俱可息，積重之勢庶幾可稍輕。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish to loosen the Eastern Depot's striking events—then the Depot's comparisons could be relaxed; once comparisons were relaxed, then both banner-servants buying events and those selling events could cease—and the accumulated weight might be lightened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that the Depot's striking-event quotas be relaxed. Relax the quotas, and both buyers and sellers of cases may cease—the accumulated weight might then be lightened.

sentences.zh: 後復切言緹騎不當遣。

translations.literal: Later he again urgently stated that brocade-clad mounted agents should not be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he again urged that brocade-clad mounted agents not be dispatched.

sentences.zh: 帝為諭東廠，言所緝止謀逆亂倫，其作奸犯科，自有司存，不宜緝，並戒錦衣校尉之橫索者。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued instructions to the Eastern Depot, saying that investigations should be limited to treason and violations of human relations; for committing offenses and breaking the law, the regular offices had jurisdiction—they should not be investigated—and he also admonished the Embroidered Guard's runner-officers against extortionate demands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed the Eastern Depot that investigations should be limited to treason and violations of human relations; ordinary crimes remained within the jurisdiction of regular offices. He also admonished the Embroidered Guard's runner-officers against extortion.

sentences.zh: 然帝倚廠衛益甚，至國亡乃已。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor relied on the Depots and Guard ever more heavily—only when the state perished did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor relied on the Depots and Guard more heavily than ever—a dependence that ended only with the dynasty's fall.

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛獄者，世所稱詔獄也。

translations.literal: The Embroidered Guard prison was what the world called the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Guard prison was what the world called the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 古者獄訟掌於司寇而已。

translations.literal: In antiquity, prisons and lawsuits were managed by the Minister of Justice alone.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, prisons and legal proceedings were handled solely by the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝始置詔獄二十六所，歷代因革不常。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han first established twenty-six imperial prisons; successive dynasties changed them irregularly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han first established twenty-six imperial prisons; later dynasties modified the system repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 五代唐明宗設侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使，乃天子自將之名。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties, Emperor Mingzong of Tang established the Commander-in-Chief of the Personal Guards' Cavalry and Infantry—the title by which the Son of Heaven personally commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties, Tang Mingzong created the post of Commander-in-Chief of the Personal Guards' Cavalry and Infantry—a title signifying the emperor's direct command of troops.

sentences.zh: 至漢有侍衛司獄，凡大事皆決焉。

translations.literal: By the time of Later Han there was the prison of the Personal Guard Office; all major cases were decided there.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han, the Personal Guard Office maintained its own prison where all major cases were adjudicated.

sentences.zh: 明錦衣衛獄近之，幽系慘酷，害無甚於此者。

translations.literal: The Ming Embroidered Guard prison resembled it—secret imprisonment, cruel and atrocious; no harm was greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Embroidered Guard prison was its counterpart—secret imprisonment of extraordinary cruelty; no institution wrought greater harm.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，天下重罪逮至京者，收系獄中，數更大獄，多使斷治，所誅殺為多。

translations.literal: In the time of the Founding Emperor, those guilty of grave offenses from across the realm who were apprehended and brought to the capital were detained in the prison; numerous major cases were repeatedly changed, and he often had them decided outright—the number executed was great.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Founding Emperor, those accused of grave crimes from across the realm were detained in the Guard prison. Repeated major trials were conducted under his direct authority, and executions were numerous.

sentences.zh: 後悉焚衛刑具，以囚送刑部審理。

translations.literal: Later he burned all the Guard's instruments of punishment and sent prisoners to the Ministry of Punishments for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Later he burned all the Guard's torture implements and sent prisoners to the Ministry of Punishments for trial.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，申明其禁，詔內外獄毋得上錦衣衛，大小咸經法司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he clarified the prohibition, decreeing that prisons inner and outer must not send cases up to the Embroidered Guard—all cases great and small must pass through the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he reaffirmed the prohibition: no case, great or small, from any prison might be sent to the Embroidered Guard—all matters must pass through the regular judicial system.

sentences.zh: 成祖幸紀綱，令治錦衣親兵，復典詔獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengzu favored Ji Gang and ordered him to command the Embroidered Guard's personal troops, restoring administration of the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu favored Ji Gang, put him in command of the Embroidered Guard's personal troops, and restored administration of the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 綱遂用其黨莊敬、袁江、王謙、李春等，緣借作奸數百千端。

translations.literal: Gang then used his partisans Zhuang Jing, Yuan Jiang, Wang Qian, Li Chun, and others, contriving and borrowing pretexts to manufacture countless hundreds and thousands of wrongdoing cases.
translations.idiomatic: Gang then deployed his partisans Zhuang Jing, Yuan Jiang, Wang Qian, and Li Chun to fabricate wrongdoing on countless pretexts.

sentences.zh: 久之，族綱，而錦衣典詔獄如故，廢洪武詔不用矣。

translations.literal: After some time, Gang's clan was exterminated—but the Embroidered Guard's administration of the imperial prison remained as before; the Hongwu decree was discarded and no longer used.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Gang's entire clan was exterminated—but the Guard's administration of the imperial prison continued unchanged. The Hongwu prohibition was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，理衛事者劉勉、徐恭皆謹飭。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Yingzong, those managing Guard affairs—Liu Mian and Xu Gong—were both strict and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingzong's early reign, Liu Mian and Xu Gong, who managed Guard affairs, were both diligent and restrained.

sentences.zh: 而王振用指揮馬順流毒天下，枷李時勉，殺劉球，皆順為之。

translations.literal: But Wang Zhen employed Commander Ma Shun, who spread poison throughout the realm—the cangue for Li Shimian, the killing of Liu Qiu—all were done by Shun.
translations.idiomatic: But Wang Zhen deployed Commander Ma Shun, whose abuses spread nationwide—the cangue for Li Shimian, the murder of Liu Qiu—all Shun's doing.

sentences.zh: 景帝初，有言官校緝事之弊者，帝切責其長，令所緝送法司，有誣罔者重罪。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Jingdi, when someone spoke of the abuses of runner-officers in intelligence work, the Emperor sharply reprimanded their chiefs and ordered that all apprehended persons be sent to the judicial offices; those who falsely incriminated others would face heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingdi's reign, when the abuses of intelligence runner-officers were brought up, the emperor sharply reprimanded their chiefs, ordered all arrestees sent to the judicial offices, and stipulated heavy penalties for false accusations.

sentences.zh: 英宗復闢，召李賢，屏左右，問時政得失。

translations.literal: When Yingzong regained the throne, he summoned Li Xian, dismissed attendants, and asked about the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong regained the throne, he summoned Li Xian in private and asked his assessment of current policy.

sentences.zh: 賢因極論官校提人之害。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon expounded at length on the harm of runner-officers' seizing people.
translations.idiomatic: Xian spoke at length about the harm wrought by runner-officers who seized people at will.

sentences.zh: 帝然其言，陰察皆實，乃召其長，戒之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented to his words, secretly investigated and found all to be true, then summoned their chiefs and admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, secretly verified the charges, and summoned the chiefs to admonish them.

sentences.zh: 已緝弋陽王敗倫事虛，復申戒之。

translations.literal: When it was found that the case of Prince Yiyang's violation of human relations was fabricated, he again issued admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: When the case alleging Prince Yiyang's incest proved fabricated, he issued further admonitions.

sentences.zh: 而是時指揮門達、鎮撫逯杲怙寵，賢亦為羅織者數矣。

translations.literal: Yet at this time Commander Men Da and Pacifier Su Gao relied on favor—Xian was also several times entrapped by fabricated charges.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Commander Men Da and Pacifier Su Gao enjoyed imperial favor at this time—and Xian himself was nearly entrapped by fabricated charges several times.

sentences.zh: 達遣旗校四出，杲又立程督並，以獲多為主。

translations.literal: Da dispatched banner-officers in all directions; Gao also established a program of supervision and parallel quotas, making high numbers of apprehensions the priority.
translations.idiomatic: Da dispatched banner-officers in all directions; Gao established parallel supervision programs, with maximizing arrests as the goal.

sentences.zh: 千戶黃麟之廣西，執御史吳禎至，索獄具二百餘副，天下朝覲官陷罪者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thousand-officer Huang Lin went to Guangxi, seized Censor Wu Zhen and brought him back, and demanded over two hundred sets of prison instruments—the number of tribute-visiting officials throughout the realm who fell into crime was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-officer Huang Lin went to Guangxi, seized Censor Wu Zhen, and demanded over two hundred sets of prison implements. Officials from across the realm visiting the capital for tribute fell into the Guard's net in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 杲死，達兼治鎮撫司。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Da also took charge of the Pacification Office.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao died, Da took over the Pacification Office as well.

sentences.zh: 構指揮使袁彬，系訊之，五毒更下，僅免。

translations.literal: He fabricated charges against Commander Yuan Bin, imprisoned and interrogated him, applied the five tortures in rotation—Bin barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: He fabricated charges against Commander Yuan Bin, imprisoned and interrogated him, and applied the five tortures in rotation. Bin barely survived.

sentences.zh: 朝官楊璡、李蕃、韓祺、李觀、包瑛、張祚、程萬鐘輩皆鋃鐺就逮，冤號道路者不可勝記。

translations.literal: Court officials Yang Jin, Li Fan, Han Qi, Li Guan, Bao Ying, Zhang Zuo, Cheng Wanzhong, and others were all shackled and taken into custody—those crying out their injustice on the roads were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials including Yang Jin, Li Fan, Han Qi, Li Guan, Bao Ying, Zhang Zuo, and Cheng Wanzhong were shackled and seized. Victims crying injustice on the roads were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 蓋自紀綱誅，其徒稍戢。

translations.literal: From the time Ji Gang was executed, his followers had somewhat restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji Gang's execution, his followers had briefly restrained themselves.

sentences.zh: 至正統時復張，天順之末禍益熾，朝野相顧不自保。

translations.literal: By the Zhengtong era they flourished again; by the end of the Tianshun era the calamity burned ever hotter—court and realm looked at one another unable to protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong era they flourished again. By the end of Tianshun the abuse raged fiercer still—court and country alike feared for their lives.

sentences.zh: 李賢雖極言之，不能救也。

translations.literal: Although Li Xian spoke against it with utmost force, he could not remedy it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Xian spoke against it with all his force, he could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫司職理獄訟，初止立一司，與外衛等。

translations.literal: The Pacification Office was charged with managing prisons and lawsuits; at first only one office was established, equal in rank to the outer guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Office managed prisons and legal proceedings. At first only one office existed, equal in rank to the outer guards.

sentences.zh: 洪武十五年添設北司，而以軍匠諸職掌屬之南鎮撫司，於是北司專理詔獄。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu the northern office was added; military artisans and various other functions were placed under the southern Pacification Office—thus the northern office exclusively managed the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 15 the northern office was added; military artisans and other functions were assigned to the southern Pacification Office, leaving the northern office exclusively in charge of the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 然大獄經訊，即送法司擬罪，未嘗具獄詞。

translations.literal: Yet after major cases were interrogated, they were at once sent to the judicial offices for sentencing—they never prepared formal case records.
translations.idiomatic: Major cases, once interrogated, were sent to the judicial offices for sentencing—but formal written verdicts were never prepared.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，始令覆奏用參語，法司益掣肘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, it was first ordered that review memorials use summary language—the judicial offices were increasingly hemmed in.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 1, review memorials were required to use summary phrasing—the judicial offices were increasingly constrained.

sentences.zh: 十四年，增鑄北司印信，一切刑獄毋關白本衛，即衛所行下者，亦逕自上請可否，衛使毋得與聞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the northern office's seal was recast and augmented—all criminal matters required no consultation with the parent Guard; even when the Guard issued orders downward, matters went straight upward to request approval or rejection—the Guard commander might not even be informed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 the northern office's seal was recast. All criminal matters bypassed the parent Guard entirely; even when the Guard issued orders, the Pacification Office reported directly upward—the Guard commander was kept out of the loop.

sentences.zh: 故鎮撫職卑而其權日重。

translations.literal: Thus though the Pacifier's rank was low, his power grew daily heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Pacifier's rank was low, his power grew steadily heavier.

sentences.zh: 初，衛獄附衛治，至門達掌問刑，又於城西設獄舍，拘繫狼籍。

translations.literal: At first the Guard prison was adjunct to the Guard administration; when Men Da took charge of interrogation, he also set up prison cells west of the city—the detainees were kept in chaotic overcrowding.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Guard prison was housed within the Guard headquarters. When Men Da took charge of interrogations, he built prison cells west of the city, where detainees were kept in chaotic overcrowding.

sentences.zh: 達敗，用御史呂洪言，毀之。

translations.literal: When Da fell, on the advice of Censor Lü Hong, they were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: After Da's downfall, on Censor Lü Hong's advice, the cells were torn down.

sentences.zh: 成化十年，都御史李賓言：「錦衣鎮撫司累獲妖書圖本，皆誕妄不經之言。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chenghua, Censor-in-Chief Li Bin said: "The Embroidered Guard Pacification Office has repeatedly seized heretical books and illustrated texts—all are absurd and unorthodox words.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 10, Censor-in-Chief Li Bin said: "The Embroidered Guard Pacification Office has repeatedly seized 'heretical books' and illustrated texts—all absurd, unorthodox nonsense.

sentences.zh: 小民無知，輒被幻惑。

translations.literal: Common people, lacking knowledge, are readily deluded and bewildered by them.
translations.idiomatic: Ignorant commoners are easily deluded by such material.

sentences.zh: 乞備錄其舊名目，榜示天下，使知畏避，免陷刑辟。」

translations.literal: I beg that their old titles be fully recorded and posted throughout the realm, so that people may know to fear and avoid them and escape falling into criminal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these titles be fully catalogued and posted throughout the realm, so people may recognize them, stay clear, and avoid criminal entrapment.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The response approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 緝事者誣告猶不止。

translations.literal: Those in intelligence work continued to lodge false accusations without cease.
translations.idiomatic: False accusations by intelligence agents did not cease.

sentences.zh: 十三年，捕甯晉人王鳳等，誣與瞽者受妖書，署偽職，並誣其鄉官知縣薛方、通判曹鼎與通謀，發卒圍其家，扌旁掠誣伏。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, they arrested Wang Feng of Ningjin and others, falsely charging them with receiving heretical books from a blind man and assuming bogus titles; they also falsely charged their local officials—Magistrate Xue Fang and Vice Magistrate Cao Ding—with conspiracy; troops were dispatched to surround their homes, and beatings and torture extracted false confessions.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 they arrested Wang Feng of Ningjin and others, falsely charging receipt of heretical texts from a blind man and assumption of bogus titles. They also implicated local officials Magistrate Xue Fang and Vice Magistrate Cao Ding in conspiracy, dispatched troops to surround their homes, and beat and tortured false confessions from them.

sentences.zh: 方、鼎家人數聲冤，下法司驗得實，坐妄報妖言，當斬。

translations.literal: Fang's and Ding's households cried out their injustice several times; the case was sent to the judicial offices, verification found the truth, and the accusers were sentenced for falsely reporting heretical talk—the penalty was decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's and Ding's families cried out their innocence. The judicial offices investigated, confirmed the fabrication, and sentenced the accusers to decapitation for falsely reporting heretical talk.

sentences.zh: 帝戒以不得戕害無辜而已，不能罪也。

translations.literal: The Emperor merely admonished them not to harm the innocent—that was all; he could not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor merely admonished them not to harm innocents—he could not bring further charges.

sentences.zh: 是年，令錦衣衛副千戶吳綬於鎮撫司同問刑。

translations.literal: That same year, Vice Thousand-officer Wu Shou of the Embroidered Guard was ordered to join the Pacification Office in conducting interrogations.
translations.idiomatic: That year Vice Thousand-officer Wu Shou of the Embroidered Guard was assigned to assist the Pacification Office in interrogations.

sentences.zh: 綬性狡險，附汪直以進。

translations.literal: Shou's nature was cunning and treacherous; he attached himself to Wang Zhi to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was cunning and treacherous; he attached himself to Wang Zhi to rise.

sentences.zh: 後知公議不容，凡文臣非罪下獄者，不復加箠楚，忤直意，黜去。

translations.literal: Later, knowing that public opinion would not tolerate it, for civil officials imprisoned without cause he no longer added beating with rods; when he thwarted Zhi's wishes, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, sensing public outrage, he stopped beating civil officials imprisoned without cause. When he crossed Zhi's will, he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 是時惟衛使朱驥持法平，治妖人獄無冤者。

translations.literal: At this time only Guard Commander Zhu Ji held the law evenly; in handling cases of heretical offenders, none were wrongly convicted.
translations.idiomatic: At this time only Guard Commander Zhu Ji administered law fairly; in heresy cases under his jurisdiction, no innocent was convicted.

sentences.zh: 詔獄下所司，獨用小杖，嘗命中使詰責，不為改。

translations.literal: At the imperial prison under his jurisdiction, he alone used small rods; he was once ordered by palace envoys to account for this and did not change.
translations.idiomatic: In the imperial prison under his authority he alone used light rods for punishment. When palace envoys ordered him to account for this, he refused to change.

sentences.zh: 世以是稱之。

translations.literal: The world praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: The world praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年，詔法司：「凡廠衛所送囚犯，從公審究，有枉即與辨理，勿拘成案。」

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi, an edict to the judicial offices said: "All prisoners sent by the Depots and Guard shall be tried and investigated openly; where there is wrong, rectify it at once—do not be bound by completed cases.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 13, an edict to the judicial offices said: "All prisoners sent by the Depots and Guard must be openly tried; where injustice is found, rectify it—do not be bound by completed verdicts.

sentences.zh: 正德時，衛使石文義與張採表裏作威福，時稱為劉瑾左右翼。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde era, Guard Commander Shi Wenyi and Zhang Cai worked inside and outside to wield power and bestow favors—the age called them Liu Jin's left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde era, Guard Commander Shi Wenyi and Zhang Cai wielded power in concert and were known as Liu Jin's left and right arms.

sentences.zh: 然文義常侍瑾，不治事，治事者高得林。

translations.literal: Yet Wenyi constantly attended Jin and did not manage affairs—he who managed affairs was Gao Delin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyi, however, constantly attended Jin and did not manage day-to-day affairs—that role fell to Gao Delin.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，文義伏誅，得林亦罷。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Wenyi was executed, and Delin was also removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was executed, Wenyi was put to death and Delin was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 其後強尼管事，復大恣，以叛誅。

translations.literal: Afterward Qiang Ni managed affairs, again indulging greatly in license, and was executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qiang Ni took charge and again indulged in gross abuses; he was executed for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，革錦衣傳奉官十六，汰旗校十五，復諭緝事官校，惟察不軌、妖言、人命、強盜重事，他詞訟及在外州縣事，毋得與。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne, he abolished sixteen specially appointed Embroidered Guard posts, reduced banner-officers by fifteen, and again instructed intelligence runner-officers that they should investigate only sedition, heretical talk, homicide, and serious robbery—they were not to involve themselves in other lawsuits or matters in outer prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne, he abolished sixteen specially appointed Guard posts, cut fifteen banner-officers, and instructed intelligence agents to investigate only sedition, heretical talk, homicide, and serious robbery—not other lawsuits or local matters outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，事多下鎮撫，鎮撫結內侍，多巧中。

translations.literal: Before long, most cases went down to the Pacification Office; the Pacification Office cultivated connections with inner eunuchs and often hit their mark by cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long most cases were routed to the Pacification Office, whose officers cultivated ties with inner eunuchs and often got their way through manipulation.

sentences.zh: 會太監崔文奸利事發，下刑部，尋以中旨送鎮撫司。

translations.literal: When Eunuch Cui Wen's corruption came to light, the case went to the Ministry of Punishments—but soon, by secret edict from within, it was sent to the Pacification Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Eunuch Cui Wen's corruption was exposed, the case went to the Ministry of Punishments—but a secret edict from within soon transferred it to the Pacification Office.

sentences.zh: 尚書林俊言：「祖宗朝以刑獄付法司，事無大小，皆聽平鞫。

translations.literal: Minister Lin Jun said: "In the time of the dynastic founders, criminal matters were entrusted to the judicial offices; matters great or small were all heard and tried impartially.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lin Jun said: "Under the dynastic founders, criminal matters were entrusted to the judicial offices; all cases, great and small, were heard and tried impartially.

sentences.zh: 自劉瑾、強尼用事，專任鎮撫司，文致冤獄，法紀大壞。

translations.literal: Since Liu Jin and Qiang Ni held power, the Pacification Office alone was relied upon—they contrived wording to produce wrongful prisons, and legal discipline was greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Jin and Qiang Ni held power, the Pacification Office has monopolized cases, fabricating wrongful imprisonments and wrecking legal discipline.

sentences.zh: 更化善治在今日，不宜復以小事撓法。」

translations.literal: Good government through reform lies in the present day—one should not again use trifling matters to disrupt the law.
translations.idiomatic: Reform and good governance depend on today—we must not let trivial matters undermine the law.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was ignored.

sentences.zh: 俊復言：「此途一開，恐後有重情，即夤緣內降以圖免，實長亂階。」

translations.literal: Jun again said: "Once this path is opened, I fear that hereafter, when serious cases arise, people will use connections to obtain secret edicts from within seeking exemption—it truly lengthens the steps of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Jun protested again: "Open this door and serious offenders will use connections to obtain secret edicts from within seeking exemption—laying the groundwork for disorder.

sentences.zh: 御史曹懷亦諫曰：「朝廷專任一鎮撫，法司可以空曹，刑官為冗員矣。」

translations.literal: Censor Cao Huai also remonstrated, saying: "If the court relies exclusively on one Pacification Office, the judicial offices may as well be empty chambers—the punishment officials become surplus posts."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cao Huai also remonstrated: "If the court relies exclusively on the Pacification Office, the judicial offices might as well be empty—the judges become redundant."

sentences.zh: 帝俱不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor heeded neither.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heeded neither protest.

sentences.zh: 六年，侍郎張璁等言：「祖宗設三法司以糾官邪，平獄訟，設東廠、錦衣衛以緝盜賊，詰奸宄。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Vice Minister Zhang Cong and others said: "The dynastic founders established the Three Judicial Offices to correct official corruption and settle lawsuits; they established the Eastern Depot and Embroidered Guard to apprehend robbers and bandits and investigate treacherous villains.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, Vice Minister Zhang Cong and others said: "The founders established the Three Judicial Offices to correct official corruption and settle lawsuits; they established the Eastern Depot and Embroidered Guard to apprehend robbers and investigate subversives.

sentences.zh: 自今貪官冤獄仍責法司，其有徇情曲法，乃聽廠衛覺察。

translations.literal: From now on, corrupt officials and wrongful prisons remain the responsibility of the judicial offices; only where there is favoritism and bending of the law should the Depots and Guard be permitted to detect it.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth corrupt officials and wrongful convictions remain the judicial offices' responsibility; only where officials bend the law through favoritism may the Depots and Guard intervene.

sentences.zh: 盜賊奸宄，仍責廠衛，亦必送法司擬罪。」

translations.literal: Robbers, bandits, and treacherous villains remain the responsibility of the Depots and Guard—but they too must send cases to the judicial offices for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers and subversives remain the Depots' and Guard's responsibility—but all cases must still be sent to the judicial offices for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 詔如議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered implementation as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the proposal be carried out.

sentences.zh: 然官校提人恣如故。

translations.literal: Yet the official guards arrested people as wantonly as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the official guards continued to arrest people with as much impunity as before.

sentences.zh: 給事中蔡經等論其害，願罷勿遣。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Cai Jing and others discussed its harm, requesting that they be abolished and not dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Cai Jing and others spoke of the harm, asking that the guards be abolished and no longer dispatched.

sentences.zh: 尚書胡世甯請從其議。

translations.literal: Minister Hu Shinan requested following their proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Hu Shinan asked that their proposal be adopted.

sentences.zh: 詹事霍韜亦言：「刑獄付三法司足矣，錦衣衛復橫撓之。

translations.literal: Senior Tutor Huo Tao also said: "Criminal prisons entrusted to the Three Judicial Offices are enough—the Embroidered Guard again brazenly interferes.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Tutor Huo Tao also said: "Criminal matters should rest with the Three Judicial Offices alone—the Embroidered Guard keeps interfering brazenly.

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武尚名節，宋太祖刑法不加衣冠，其後忠義之徒爭死效節。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Guangwu of Han esteemed reputation and integrity; Emperor Taizu of Song did not apply penal law to officials in court dress—afterward men of loyalty and righteousness competed to die upholding integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Emperor Guangwu of Han prized reputation and integrity, and Emperor Taizu of Song would not apply penal law to officials in court dress—after which loyal men competed to die upholding their principles.

sentences.zh: 夫士大夫有罪下刑曹，辱矣。

translations.literal: When scholar-officials with guilt are handed to the punishment offices, it is humiliating enough.
translations.idiomatic: Handing a scholar-official over to the punishment offices when he is guilty is humiliation enough.

sentences.zh: 有重罪，廢之、誅之可也，乃使官校眾執之，脫冠裳，就桎梏。

translations.literal: If there is a grave offense, demoting or executing him would suffice—yet they make many official guards seize him, strip off cap and robes, and put on shackles.
translations.idiomatic: For grave offenses, dismissal or execution would suffice—yet they set many official guards on him, strip off his cap and robes, and put him in shackles.

sentences.zh: 朝列清班，暮幽犴獄，剛心壯氣，銷折殆盡。

translations.literal: In the morning he ranks among the pure court assembly; by evening he is in the dark prison—the firm heart and strong spirit are worn away almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Standing in the morning among the court's senior ranks, by evening confined in a dark prison—the firm heart and strong spirit are broken almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 及覆案非罪，即冠帶立朝班，武夫捍卒指目之曰：『某，吾辱之，某，吾系執之。』

translations.literal: When review finds no crime and he at once stands in court ranks with cap and belt, soldiers and guards point at him and say: 'So-and-so—I humiliated him; so-and-so—I bound and seized him.'
translations.idiomatic: When review clears him of wrongdoing and he stands again in court with cap and belt, soldiers and guards point and say: 'That one—I humiliated him; that one—I bound and seized him.'

sentences.zh: 小人無所忌憚，君子遂致易行。

translations.literal: Base men are without fear or restraint; gentlemen consequently come to shrink from proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men lose all restraint; gentlemen in turn shrink from standing firm.

sentences.zh: 此豪傑所以興山林之思，而變故罕仗節之士也。

translations.literal: This is why bold spirits turn their thoughts to life in the mountains and forests, and in times of upheaval few are found who uphold integrity.
translations.idiomatic: This is why bold spirits dream of retreat to the mountains, and in crisis few are found who will stand by their principles.

sentences.zh: 願自今東廠勿與朝儀，錦衣衛勿典刑獄。

translations.literal: I wish that from now on the Eastern Depot not participate in court ceremony, and the Embroidered Guard not administer criminal prisons.
