translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter the Eastern Depot be kept from court ceremony, and the Embroidered Guard from administering criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 士大夫罪謫廢誅，勿加笞杖鎖梏，以養廉恥，振人心，勵士節。」

translations.literal: When scholar-officials' crimes warrant exile, dismissal, or execution, do not add beating with rods, cudgels, or shackles—to nurture integrity and shame, stir men's hearts, and encourage official steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: When scholar-officials deserve exile, dismissal, or death, spare them the rod and shackles—to nurture integrity, lift men's spirits, and encourage steadfast service.

sentences.zh: 帝以韜出位妄言，不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering Tao's speech beyond his station and reckless, did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deemed Tao's speech presumptuous and reckless, and rejected it.

sentences.zh: 祖制，凡朝會，廠衛率屬及校尉五百名，列侍奉天門下糾儀。

translations.literal: By ancestral regulation, at every court assembly the Depots and Guard led subordinates and five hundred guard officers, arrayed to attend below the Gate of Heavenly Succession and maintain ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: By ancestral regulation, at every court assembly the Depots and Guard led their subordinates—five hundred guard officers arrayed below the Gate of Heavenly Succession to maintain ceremonial order.

sentences.zh: 凡失儀者，即褫衣冠，執下鎮撫司獄，杖之乃免，故韜言及之。

translations.literal: Whoever breached ceremony was at once stripped of cap and robes, seized and sent down to the Pacification Office prison, beaten with rods and then released—hence Tao spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who breached ceremony was stripped of cap and robes, dragged to the Pacification Office prison, beaten, and only then released—this is what Tao had in mind.

sentences.zh: 迨萬歷時，失儀者始不付獄，罰俸而已。

translations.literal: By the Wanli era, those who breached ceremony were at first not sent to prison; salary deduction alone sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: By the Wanli reign, offenders against ceremony were no longer sent to prison—they were fined in salary only.

sentences.zh: 世宗銜張鶴齡、延齡，奸人劉東山等乃誣二人毒魘咒詛。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor harbored resentment toward Zhang Heling and Yanling; wicked men such as Liu Dongshan then falsely accused the two of poisoning, bewitching, and cursing.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor still resented Zhang Heling and Yanling; schemers such as Liu Dongshan then falsely accused the two of poisoning, witchcraft, and cursing.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下詔獄，東山因株引素所不快者。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and sent them to the imperial prison; Dongshan thereby implicated by association those he had always disliked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and sent them to the imperial prison; Dongshan used the case to implicate everyone he had long resented.

sentences.zh: 衛使王佐探得其情，論以誣罔法反坐。

translations.literal: Guard Commander Wang Zuo investigated and obtained the facts, applying the law of counter-charge for false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Guard Commander Wang Zuo uncovered the truth and applied the counter-charge law for false accusation.

sentences.zh: 佐乃枷東山等闕門外，不及旬悉死，人以佐比牟斌。

translations.literal: Zuo then cangued Dongshan and the others outside the palace gate; within less than ten days all died—people compared Zuo to Mou Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo then placed Dongshan and the others in the cangue outside the palace gate; within ten days all were dead—people compared him to Mou Bin.

sentences.zh: 牟斌者，弘治中指揮也。

translations.literal: Mou Bin was a guard officer in the Hongzhi reign.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Bin had been a guard officer under the Hongzhi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 李夢陽論延齡兄弟不法事，下獄，斌傅輕比，得不死云。

translations.literal: When Li Mengyang discussed the Yanling brothers' unlawful conduct and was imprisoned, Bin applied a lighter statute comparison, so he did not die, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mengyang spoke out against the Yanling brothers' misconduct and was imprisoned, Bin applied a lighter statute and saved his life, it is said.

sentences.zh: 世宗中年，衛使陸炳為忮，與嚴嵩比，而傾夏言。

translations.literal: In the Shizong Emperor's middle years, Guard Commander Lu Bing was jealous and malicious, aligned with Yan Song, and overthrew Xia Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shizong Emperor's middle years, Guard Commander Lu Bing was jealous and ruthless, allied with Yan Song, and helped bring down Xia Yan.

sentences.zh: 然帝數興大獄，而炳多保全之，故士大夫不疾炳。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor repeatedly launched major prosecutions, while Bing often preserved people—therefore scholar-officials did not resent Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor repeatedly launched major prosecutions, and Bing often shielded the accused—so scholar-officials did not turn against him.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，建言及忤礦稅榼者，輒下詔獄。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, those who remonstrated or opposed mining taxes and tax monopolies were promptly sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli, anyone who remonstrated or resisted mining taxes and tax monopolies was promptly sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 刑科給事中楊應文言：「監司守令及齊民被逮者百五十餘人，雖已打問，未送法司，獄禁森嚴，水火不入，疫癘之氣，充斥囹圄。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yang Yingwen of the Penal Section said: "Surveillance commissioners, magistrates, and common people seized number more than one hundred fifty; though already interrogated under torture, they have not been sent to the judicial offices. Prison confinement is stern—even water and fire may not enter; pestilential miasma fills the jail.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yang Yingwen of the Penal Section reported: "More than one hundred fifty surveillance commissioners, magistrates, and ordinary people have been seized. Though tortured, none have reached the judicial offices. The prisons are sealed tight—no provisions or warmth get in—and pestilence fills the cells.

sentences.zh: 衛使駱思恭亦言：「熱審歲舉，俱在小滿前，今二年不行。

translations.literal: Guard Commander Luo Sigong also said: "The annual hot-weather review is held each year, all before Grain Full—now two years have passed without holding it.
translations.idiomatic: Guard Commander Luo Sigong also reported: "The annual summer prison review is supposed to be held before Grain Full—it has not been held for two years.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫司監犯且二百，多拋瓦聲冤。」

translations.literal: Prisoners under Pacification Office supervision number nearly two hundred; many throw tiles crying out their innocence."
translations.idiomatic: Nearly two hundred prisoners languish in the Pacification Office; many throw tiles from their cells crying that they are innocent."

sentences.zh: 鎮撫司陸逵亦言：「獄囚怨恨，有持刀斷指者。」

translations.literal: Pacification Office officer Lu Kui also said: "Prisoners filled with resentment—some have taken knives and severed fingers."
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Office officer Lu Kui also reported: "Prisoners, seething with resentment, have taken knives and cut off their own fingers."

sentences.zh: 俱不報。

translations.literal: Neither was answered.
translations.idiomatic: None of these memorials received a response.

sentences.zh: 然是時，告訐風衰，大臣被錄者寡。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the climate of denunciation had waned; few great ministers were taken for recording.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by then the fever of informers had cooled, and few senior ministers were arrested.

sentences.zh: 其末年，稍寬逮繫諸臣，而錦衣獄漸清矣。

translations.literal: In its final years, arrest and imprisonment of various officials was somewhat relaxed, and the Embroidered Guard prison gradually cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's last years, arrests of officials eased somewhat, and the Embroidered Guard prison gradually emptied.

sentences.zh: 田爾耕、許顯純在熹宗時為魏忠賢義子，其黨孫雲鶴、楊寰、崔應元佐之，拷楊漣、左光鬥輩，坐贓比較，立限嚴督之。

translations.literal: Tian Ergeng and Xu Xianchun in the Xizong reign were adopted sons of Wei Zhongxian; their faction members Sun Yunhe, Yang Huan, and Cui Yingyuan assisted them in torturing Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, and others—fixing them for corruption under statute comparison, setting deadlines and sternly supervising.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xizong Emperor, Tian Ergeng and Xu Xianchun were Wei Zhongxian's adopted sons; their allies Sun Yunhe, Yang Huan, and Cui Yingyuan helped torture Yang Lian, Zuo Guangdou, and others—charging them with corruption under statutory comparison, setting strict deadlines and supervising relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 兩日為一限，輸金不中程者，受全刑。

translations.literal: Two days formed one deadline; those who failed to pay gold to schedule received the full punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Every two days brought a new deadline; anyone who failed to pay the demanded sum on time received the full suite of tortures.

sentences.zh: 全刑者曰械，曰鐐，曰棍，曰拶，曰夾棍。

translations.literal: Full punishments were called: restraint devices, leg irons, cudgels, finger presses, and leg-press boards.
translations.idiomatic: The full suite comprised restraints, leg irons, cudgels, finger presses, and leg-press boards.

sentences.zh: 五毒備具，呼ＢＫ聲沸然，血肉潰爛，宛轉求死不得。

translations.literal: The five tortures were all prepared; cries of lamentation boiled over, flesh and blood putrefied and rotted—they twisted in agony begging for death yet could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: All five tortures were deployed; wails filled the air, flesh and blood putrefied, and victims twisted in agony begging for death they could not obtain.

sentences.zh: 顯純叱吒自若，然必伺忠賢旨，忠賢所遣聽記者未至，不敢訊也。

translations.literal: Xianchun shouted commands as if at ease, yet he had to await Wei Zhongxian's intent—if the note-taker dispatched by Zhongxian had not arrived, he dared not interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: Xianchun barked orders with casual ease, but always waited on Wei Zhongxian's word—he dared not begin interrogation until Zhongxian's note-taker had arrived.

sentences.zh: 一夕，令諸囚分舍宿。

translations.literal: One evening, he ordered all prisoners to lodge separately by cell.
translations.idiomatic: One evening he ordered the prisoners separated into individual cells for the night.

sentences.zh: 於是獄卒曰：「今夕有當壁挺者。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the jailers said: "Tonight there will be one due for the wall pole.
translations.idiomatic: The jailers then said: "Tonight someone gets the wall pole."

sentences.zh: 壁挺，獄中言死也。

translations.literal: Wall pole—in prison speech, death.
translations.idiomatic: Wall pole"—prison slang for death.

sentences.zh: 明日，漣死，光鬥等次第皆鎖頭拉死。

translations.literal: The next day Lian died; Guangdou and the others in turn were all strangled to death with the lock-head method.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Lian died; Guangdou and the others were strangled to death in succession with the lock-head rope.

sentences.zh: 每一人死，停數日，葦席裹屍出牢戶，蟲蛆腐體。

translations.literal: Each time one died, they paused several days, wrapped the corpse in reed matting and carried it out through the prison door—maggots eating the putrefying body.
translations.idiomatic: After each death they waited several days, then wrapped the corpse in a reed mat and carried it out through the prison door, maggots already feasting on the rotting flesh.

sentences.zh: 獄中事祕，其家人或不知死日。

translations.literal: Prison affairs were secret; their families sometimes did not know the day of death.
translations.idiomatic: Prison affairs were kept secret; families sometimes never learned the day of death.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝擒戮逆黨，冤死家子弟望獄門稽顙哀號，為文以祭。

translations.literal: When the Zhuanglie Emperor captured and executed the rebel faction, sons and younger brothers of the wrongfully dead kowtowed at the prison gate wailing in grief, composing texts to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhuanglie Emperor seized and executed the rebel faction, sons and younger brothers of the wrongfully dead prostrated themselves at the prison gate, wailing and composing memorial texts of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之惻然。

translations.literal: The Emperor, hearing this, was deeply moved with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved when he heard of it.

sentences.zh: 自劉瑾創立枷，錦衣獄常用之。

translations.literal: Since Liu Jin created the standing cangue, the Embroidered Guard prison commonly used it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Jin invented the standing cangue, the Embroidered Guard prison used it routinely.

sentences.zh: 神宗時，御史朱應轂具言其慘，請除之。

translations.literal: In the Shenzong reign, Censor Zhu Yinggu fully described its cruelty and requested its abolition.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shenzong Emperor, Censor Zhu Yinggu described its brutality in full and asked that it be abolished.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His request was ignored.

sentences.zh: 至忠賢，益為大枷，又設斷脊、墜指、刺心之刑。

translations.literal: Under Zhongxian it became an even larger cangue; he also established punishments of breaking the spine, dropping fingers, and piercing the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongxian the cangue grew even larger, and new tortures were added—breaking the spine, smashing fingers, and piercing the heart.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝問左右：「立枷何為？」

translations.literal: The Zhuanglie Emperor asked those around him: "What is the standing cangue for?
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanglie Emperor asked his attendants: "What is the standing cangue for?

sentences.zh: 王體乾對曰：「以罪鉅奸大憝耳。」

translations.literal: Wang Tiqian replied: "To punish great villains and arch-evildoers."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tiqian replied: "For punishing the greatest traitors and evildoers."

sentences.zh: 帝愀然曰：「雖如此，終可憫。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said somberly: "Even so, it remains pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said darkly: "Even so, it remains pitiable."

sentences.zh: 忠賢為頸縮。

translations.literal: Zhongxian shrank his neck.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian visibly cringed.

sentences.zh: 東廠之禍，至忠賢而極。

translations.literal: The calamity of the Eastern Depot reached its extreme with Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Depot's tyranny reached its peak under Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 然廠衛未有不相結者，獄情輕重，廠能得於內。

translations.literal: Yet never were the Depots and Guard unconnected; the weight of prison cases the Depots could obtain from within.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Depots and Guard were always intertwined—the Depots could sway the severity of cases from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 而外廷有扞格者，衛則東西兩司房訪緝之，北司拷問之，鍛煉周內，始送法司。

translations.literal: When the outer court had obstructers, the Guard's eastern and western bureau rooms investigated and apprehended them, the northern bureau tortured and interrogated them, forged evidence to complete the case within, then only then sent them to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: When officials in the outer court resisted, the Guard's eastern and western bureau rooms tracked them down, the northern bureau tortured confessions out of them, fabricated evidence to close the case, and only then sent them to the judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 即東廠所獲，亦必移鎮撫再鞫，而後刑部得擬其罪。

translations.literal: Even those captured by the Eastern Depot had to be transferred to the Pacification Office for re-interrogation before the Ministry of Punishments could propose their sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Even prisoners seized by the Eastern Depot had to be transferred to the Pacification Office for re-interrogation before the Ministry of Punishments could fix their sentences.

sentences.zh: 故廠勢強，則衛附之，廠勢稍弱，則衛反氣淩其上。

translations.literal: Therefore when Depot power was strong, the Guard attached to it; when Depot power weakened slightly, the Guard in turn arrogantly looked down on those above.
translations.idiomatic: When the Depots were strong, the Guard attached itself to them; when Depot power waned, the Guard in turn lorded it over them.

sentences.zh: 陸炳緝司禮李彬、東廠馬廣陰事，皆至死，以炳得內閣嵩意。

translations.literal: Lu Bing investigated secret matters of Li Bin of the Directorate of Ceremonial and Ma Guang of the Eastern Depot—both were put to death—because Bing obtained the favor of the Grand Secretariat's Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bing investigated secret misconduct by Li Bin of the Directorate of Ceremonial and Ma Guang of the Eastern Depot—both men were executed—because he had the backing of Yan Song and the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及後中官愈重，閣勢日輕。

translations.literal: Later inner eunuchs grew ever heavier in influence; Grand Secretariat power daily grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as eunuchs grew ever more powerful, the Grand Secretariat's influence steadily waned.

sentences.zh: 閣臣反比廠為之下，而衛使無不競趨廠門，甘為役隸矣。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries in turn ranked below the Depots; Guard commanders all competed to rush to the Depot gates, willing to serve as menials.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries now ranked below the Depots, and Guard commanders competed to grovel at the Depot gates, content to serve as menials.

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛升授勳衛、任子、科目、功升，凡四途。

translations.literal: Embroidered Guard promotion and appointment had four paths: merit guard, appointment by son's privilege, examination subject, and promotion by merit.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion within the Embroidered Guard followed four paths: hereditary merit guard, appointment by privilege of office, examination graduate, and promotion for service.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖以前，文臣子弟多不屑就。

translations.literal: Before the Jiajing reign, sons of civil officials mostly disdained taking such posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jiajing, sons of civil officials mostly scorned such appointments.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，劉守有以名臣子掌衛，其後皆樂居之。

translations.literal: At the start of Wanli, Liu Shouyou, son of a distinguished minister, headed the Guard; thereafter all were glad to hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli, Liu Shouyou—a distinguished minister's son—headed the Guard; thereafter everyone was eager for the post.

sentences.zh: 士大夫與往還，獄急時，頗賴其力。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials maintained contact with them; when prison matters were urgent, they relied considerably on their power.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials cultivated ties with them, and in urgent prison cases often depended on their help.

sentences.zh: 守有子承禧及吳孟明其著者也。

translations.literal: Shouyou's son Chengxi and Wu Mengming were among the notable ones.
translations.idiomatic: Notable examples include Shouyou's son Chengxi and Wu Mengming.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝疑羣下，王德化掌東廠，以慘刻輔之，孟明掌衛印，時有縱舍，然觀望廠意不敢違。

translations.literal: The Zhuanglie Emperor distrusted his officials; Wang Dehua headed the Eastern Depot, assisted by men of cruel severity; Mengming held the Guard seal—at times he showed leniency, yet watched the Depot's intent and dared not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanglie Emperor distrusted his court; Wang Dehua ran the Eastern Depot with brutal assistants, while Mengming held the Guard seal—he sometimes showed mercy, but always watched the Depot's mood and never dared defy it.

sentences.zh: 而鎮撫樑清宏、喬可用朋比為惡。

translations.literal: Pacification officers Liang Qinghong and Qiao Keyong banded together in evil.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification officers Liang Qinghong and Qiao Keyong formed a vicious partnership.

sentences.zh: 凡縉紳之門，必有數人往來蹤跡，故常晏起早闔，毋敢偶語。

translations.literal: At every gentry and official's gate there were invariably several men coming and going on surveillance—therefore they often stayed up late and rose early to close doors, not daring to speak casually.
translations.idiomatic: Spies constantly tracked comings and goings at every official's gate, so households stayed up late and barred their doors early, afraid even to whisper.

sentences.zh: 旗校過門，如被大盜，官為囊橐，均分其利。

translations.literal: When banner guards passed a gate it was like being robbed by great bandits—officials served as their purses, dividing the profits equally.
translations.idiomatic: When banner guards passed a gate it was like a major robbery—officials became their purses, splitting the loot.

sentences.zh: 京城中奸細潛入，傭夫販子陰為流賊所遣，無一舉發，而高門富豪跼蹐無甯居。

translations.literal: Spies infiltrated the capital; laborers and peddlers secretly served as agents of bandits—not one was exposed, while great families and the wealthy lived in cramped anxiety without peaceful dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Spies infiltrated the capital; laborers and peddlers secretly worked as bandits' agents—not one plot was uncovered, while great families lived in constant dread.

sentences.zh: 其徒黠者恣行請託，稍拂其意，飛誣立構，摘竿牘片字，株連至十數人。

translations.literal: Their shrewdest operatives freely practiced entreaty and patronage; slightly crossing their will, they instantly fabricated accusations, plucking a word or phrase from a letter and implicating by association up to a dozen people.
translations.idiomatic: Their cleverest agents traded freely in favors; cross them slightly and accusations flew—in a single phrase from a letter they would implicate a dozen people.

sentences.zh: 姜採、熊開元下獄，帝諭掌衛駱養性潛殺之。

translations.literal: Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan were imprisoned; the Emperor instructed Guard Commander Luo Yangxing to kill them secretly.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan were imprisoned, the emperor ordered Guard Commander Luo Yangxing to kill them in secret.

sentences.zh: 養性泄上語，且言：「二臣當死，宜付所司，書其罪，使天下明知。

translations.literal: Yangxing leaked the imperial words and moreover said: "The two ministers deserve death—they should be handed to the appropriate office, their crimes written down, so all under Heaven clearly know.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxing disclosed the emperor's order and argued: "These two ministers deserve death—but let the proper office handle it, record their crimes, and make the world see clearly.

sentences.zh: 若陰使臣殺之，天下後世謂陛下何如主？」

translations.literal: If you secretly have this minister kill them, what kind of ruler will all under Heaven and posterity say Your Majesty is?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty secretly has me kill them, what will the world and posterity say of you as a ruler?

sentences.zh: 會大臣多為採等言，遂得長系。

translations.literal: As many great ministers spoke on behalf of Cai and the others, they were thereby long imprisoned instead.
translations.idiomatic: Many senior ministers spoke up for Cai and the others, and the two were held in long-term detention instead.

sentences.zh: 此養性之可稱者，然他事肆虐亦多矣。

translations.literal: This is what was praiseworthy in Yangxing—yet in other matters his rampages were also many.
translations.idiomatic: This was to Yangxing's credit—yet in other matters he rampaged just as freely.

sentences.zh: 錦衣舊例有功賞，惟緝不軌者當之。

translations.literal: The Embroidered Guard's old regulation had merit rewards—only those who apprehended subversives were entitled.
translations.idiomatic: Under old Embroidered Guard practice, merit rewards were reserved for those who apprehended subversives.

sentences.zh: 其後冒濫無紀，所報百無一實。

translations.literal: Afterward fraud overflowed without limit; of reports made, not one in a hundred was real.
translations.idiomatic: Later the system became corrupt beyond reckoning—not one report in a hundred was genuine.

sentences.zh: 吏民重困，而廠衛題請輒從。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners were heavily burdened, yet memorial requests from Depots and Guard were promptly granted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners were crushed under the burden, yet the Depots' and Guard's reward petitions were routinely approved.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，給事中歐陽一敬極言其弊，言：「緝事員役，其勢易逞，而又各類計所獲功次，以為升授。

translations.literal: At the start of Longqing, Supervising Secretary Ouyang Yijing spoke urgently of its abuses, saying: "Investigation officers and operatives—their power is easily abused—and moreover each category tallies captures for merit ranking, using them for promotion and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing, Supervising Secretary Ouyang Yijing condemned the abuses at length: "Investigation officers hold power that invites abuse, and each unit tallies arrests to rack up merit ranks for promotion.

sentences.zh: 則憑可逞之勢，邀必獲之功，枉人利己，何所不至。

translations.literal: Then relying on power easily abused, they seek merit that must be obtained—wronging others to benefit themselves—what would they not do?
translations.idiomatic: Given power they can abuse and quotas they must fill, they frame the innocent for their own gain—there is nothing they will not do.

sentences.zh: 有盜經出首倖免，故令多引平民以充數者；

translations.literal: There were cases where a thief, having turned himself in, was spared—so they deliberately had him implicate many commoners to fill the quota;
translations.idiomatic: Thieves who turned themselves in and were spared were made to implicate commoners to pad the numbers;

sentences.zh: 有括家囊為盜贓，挾市豪以為證者；

translations.literal: there were cases where they seized a household's entire purse as stolen goods and coerced market bullies to serve as witnesses;
translations.idiomatic: households were stripped of everything as stolen goods, with market bullies coerced as witnesses;

sentences.zh: 有潛構圖書，懷挾偽批，用妖言假印之律相誣陷者；

translations.literal: there were cases where they secretly fabricated texts, concealed forged endorsements, and used statutes on heterodox speech and false seals to frame people;
translations.idiomatic: texts were planted, forged endorsements planted on victims, and they were charged under laws against seditious writings and false seals;

sentences.zh: 或姓名相類，朦朧見收；

translations.literal: or names were similar and people were vaguely seized;
translations.idiomatic: similar names led to vague arrests;

sentences.zh: 父訴子孝，坐以忤逆。

translations.literal: a father pleaded his son's filial piety, yet the son was convicted of unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: a father pleaded his son's filial devotion, yet the son was convicted of unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 所以被訪之家，諺稱為剗，毒害可知矣。

translations.literal: Therefore households subjected to investigation were proverbially called 'plowed under'—the poison can be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: Households subjected to investigation were proverbially 'plowed under'—the devastation speaks for itself.

sentences.zh: 乞自今定制，機密重情，事幹憲典者，廠衛如故題請。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on a fixed regulation be made: for secret and weighty cases touching fundamental law, Depots and Guard may memorialize as before.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a fixed rule be established: for secret and serious cases touching fundamental law, the Depots and Guard may petition as before.

sentences.zh: 其情罪不明，未經讞審，必待法司詳擬成獄之後，方與紀功。

translations.literal: Where facts and guilt are unclear, and judgment trial has not yet been held, reward for merit must await the judicial offices' detailed proposal and completed case—only then should merit be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Where guilt is unclear and no trial has been held, merit rewards must wait until the judicial offices have fully tried the case and closed it.

sentences.zh: 仍敕兵、刑二部勘問明白，請旨升賞。

translations.literal: Still order the Ministries of War and Punishments to investigate clearly, then request imperial instruction for promotion and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Have the Ministries of War and Punishments investigate thoroughly, then seek imperial approval for promotion and reward.

sentences.zh: 或經緝拿未成獄者，不得虛冒比擬，及他詞訟不得概涉，以侵有司之事。

translations.literal: Or cases investigated and seized but not yet completed may not receive false merit comparison; other lawsuits may not be broadly implicated, encroaching on the regular officials' affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Arrests that have not yet become completed cases must not yield inflated merit claims; unrelated lawsuits must not be swept in, encroaching on regular officials' jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 如獄未成，而官校及鎮撫司拷打傷重，或至死者，許法司參治。

translations.literal: If a case is not yet complete yet official guards and the Pacification Office beat someone severely or even to death, allow the judicial offices to impeach and punish.
translations.idiomatic: If guards or the Pacification Office severely beat prisoners—or kill them—before a case is closed, let the judicial offices investigate and punish.

sentences.zh: 法司容隱扶同，則聽科臣並參。

translations.literal: If the judicial offices conceal and abet, then allow supervising secretaries jointly to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: If the judicial offices cover for them, let supervising secretaries join in impeachment.

sentences.zh: 如此則功必覆實，訪必當事，而刑無冤濫。」

translations.literal: Thus merit would necessarily be verified; investigation would necessarily hit the mark; and punishment would be without wrongful excess.
translations.idiomatic: Then merit claims would be verified, investigations would target real crimes, and punishment would be free of wrongful excess.

sentences.zh: 時不能用也。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 內官同法司錄囚，始於正統六年，命何文淵、王文審行在疑獄，敕同內官興安。

translations.literal: Inner eunuchs jointly reviewing prisoners with the judicial offices began in the sixth year of Zhengtong—the order went to He Wenyuan and Wang Wen to try doubtful cases at the mobile capital, instructing Inner Eunuch Xing An to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs reviewing prisoners alongside the judicial offices began in Zhengtong year 6, when He Wenyuan and Wang Wen were ordered to try doubtful cases at the mobile capital, joined by Inner Eunuch Xing An.

sentences.zh: 周忱、郭瑾往南京，敕亦如之。

translations.literal: Zhou Chen and Guo Jin went to Nanjing; the edict was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Chen and Guo Jin went to Nanjing, the same instruction applied.

sentences.zh: 時雖未定五年大審之制，而南北內官得與三法司刑獄矣。

translations.literal: Although the system of great review every five years was not yet fixed, inner eunuchs of north and south could participate with the three judicial offices in criminal prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Although the five-year great review system was not yet established, inner eunuchs in both capitals were already joining the three judicial offices in handling criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年，命太監王誠會三法司審錄在京刑獄，不及南京者，因災創舉也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai, eunuch Wang Cheng was ordered to join the three judicial offices in reviewing and recording capital criminal prisoners — not extending to Nanjing; this was first undertaken because of a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jingtai (1455), eunuch Wang Cheng was ordered to join the three judicial offices in reviewing capital prisoners—Nanjing was not included; the practice began in response to a natural disaster.

sentences.zh: 成化八年，命司禮太監王高、少監宋文毅兩京會審，而各省恤刑之差，亦以是歲而定。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua, Director of Ceremonies eunuch Wang Gao and Vice Director Song Wenyi were ordered to conduct joint reviews in both capitals; the dispatch of compassionate-review envoys to the provinces was also fixed in this year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chenghua (1472), Director of Ceremonies eunuch Wang Gao and Vice Director Song Wenyi were ordered to conduct joint reviews in both capitals; the system of dispatching compassionate-review officials to the provinces was also established that year.

sentences.zh: 十七年辛卯，命太監懷恩同法司錄囚。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the xinmao year, eunuch Huai'en was ordered to join the judicial offices in recording prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1481), the xinmao year, eunuch Huai'en was ordered to join the judicial offices in recording prisoners.

sentences.zh: 其後審錄必以丙辛之歲。

translations.literal: Thereafter review recordings were always conducted in bing and xin years.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, review recordings were always conducted in years with the bing or xin stem.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年不遣內官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi, no inner eunuchs were dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Hongzhi (1496), no inner eunuchs were dispatched.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以給事中丘俊言，復命會審。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, on the memorial of Supervising Secretary Qiu Jun, joint review was again ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1500), on Supervising Secretary Qiu Jun's memorial, joint review was restored.

sentences.zh: 凡大審錄，齎敕張黃蓋於大理寺，為三尺壇，中坐，三法司左右坐，御史、郎中以下捧牘立，唯諾趨走惟謹。

translations.literal: Whenever a great review recording took place, they carried the imperial command and spread a yellow canopy at the Court of Judicial Review, set up a three-foot altar, and sat in the center; the three judicial offices sat to left and right; censors, bureau directors, and those below held documents standing, responding and hurrying with utmost deference.
translations.idiomatic: At every great review, the envoy carried the imperial command and raised a yellow canopy at the Court of Judicial Review. A three-foot altar was set up; the eunuch sat in the center, the three judicial offices to his left and right, while censors and bureau directors below stood holding documents, answering and scurrying with utmost deference.

sentences.zh: 三法司視成案，有所出入輕重，俱視中官意，不敢忤也。

translations.literal: The three judicial offices looked at completed cases; any discrepancy in severity all followed the inner eunuch's wishes — they dared not oppose.
translations.idiomatic: The three judicial offices reviewed completed cases, but any adjustment in severity followed the inner eunuch's wishes—they dared not dissent.

sentences.zh: 成化時，會審有弟助兄鬥，因毆殺人者，太監黃賜欲從末減。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua era, at joint review there was one who helped his elder brother in a fight and thereby beat someone to death; eunuch Huang Ci wished to apply the least reduction.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign, a joint review case involved a younger brother who aided his elder in a brawl and thereby beat a man to death; eunuch Huang Ci wished to apply the lightest possible sentence.

sentences.zh: 尚書陸瑜等持不可，賜曰：「同室鬥者，尚被髮纓冠救之，況其兄乎？」

translations.literal: Minister Lu Yu and others insisted it could not be done; Ci said: "For those who fight within the same household, one even loosens the hair and adjusts the cap to save them — how much more for his elder brother?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lu Yu and others objected, but Ci said, "When people of the same household fight, custom allows one to loosen the hair and adjust the cap to intervene—how much more when it is one's elder brother?"

sentences.zh: 瑜等不敢難，卒為屈法。

translations.literal: Yu and the others dared not dispute further; in the end the law was bent.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and the others dared not press the point; in the end the law was bent to accommodate him.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十四年大審，御史曹學程以建言久系，羣臣請宥，皆不聽。

translations.literal: At the great review in the thirty-fourth year of Wanli, Censor Cao Xuecheng, long imprisoned for remonstrance, was sought for pardon by the officials — all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: At the great review of the thirty-fourth year of Wanli (1606), Censor Cao Xuecheng had long been imprisoned for remonstrance; officials petitioned for his pardon, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎沈應文署尚書事，合院寺之長，以書抵太監陳矩，請寬學程罪。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Shen Yingwen, acting as Minister, together with the heads of the commissions and courts, wrote to eunuch Chen Ju requesting leniency for Xuecheng's offense.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Shen Yingwen, acting as Minister, together with the heads of the commissions and courts, wrote to eunuch Chen Ju asking that Xuecheng's sentence be lightened.

sentences.zh: 然後會審，獄具，署名同奏。

translations.literal: Only then was joint review held; the case was complete, signatures affixed, and memorial submitted together.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was joint review held; when the case was complete, all signed and submitted a joint memorial.

sentences.zh: 矩復密啟，言學程母老可念。

translations.literal: Ju again secretly reported, saying Xuecheng's mother was aged and pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ju then secretly reported that Xuecheng's mother was elderly and deserving of pity.

sentences.zh: 帝意解，釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind relented, and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 其事甚美，而監權之重如此。

translations.literal: The affair was quite admirable, yet such was the weight of eunuch power.
translations.idiomatic: The outcome was admirable, yet it shows how heavy eunuch power had become.

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛使亦得與法司午門外鞫囚，及秋後承天門外會審，而大審不與也。

translations.literal: The Embroidered Guard commissioner could also join the judicial offices outside the Meridian Gate to interrogate prisoners, and after autumn outside Chengtian Gate for joint review — but not at the great review.
translations.idiomatic: The Embroidered Guard commissioner could also join judicial offices outside the Meridian Gate to interrogate prisoners, and after autumn for joint review outside Chengtian Gate—but not at the great review.

sentences.zh: 每歲決囚後，圖諸囚罪狀於衛之外垣，令人觀省。

translations.literal: Each year after sentences were decided, the crimes of all prisoners were painted on the outer wall of the Guard for people to view and reflect.
translations.idiomatic: Each year after sentences were handed down, the crimes of all condemned prisoners were painted on the Guard's outer wall for public viewing.

sentences.zh: 內臣曾奉命審錄者，死則於墓寢畫壁，南面坐，旁列法司堂上官，及御史、刑部郎引囚鞠躬聽命狀，示後世為榮觀焉。

translations.literal: Inner eunuchs who had been ordered to conduct review recordings — when they died, at their tomb enclosure they painted on the wall, seated facing south, with chiefs of the judicial offices to the side, and censors and Ministry of Justice bureau directors leading prisoners bowing to receive commands — showing later generations a sight of glory.
translations.idiomatic: Inner eunuchs who had conducted review recordings, when they died, had their tomb enclosures painted with scenes of themselves seated facing south, judicial chiefs arrayed beside them, and censors and Ministry of Justice bureau directors leading prisoners forward to bow and receive orders—a spectacle of glory for posterity.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，命內官臨斬強盜宋全。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua, an inner eunuch was ordered to supervise the execution of the bandit Song Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua (1466), an inner eunuch was ordered to supervise the execution of the bandit Song Quan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，內臣犯法，詔免逮問，唯下司禮監治。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era, when inner eunuchs broke the law, an edict exempted them from arrest and inquiry; they were sent only to the Directorate of Ceremonials for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign, when inner eunuchs broke the law, edicts exempted them from arrest and formal inquiry; they were punished only within the Directorate of Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書林俊言：「宮府一體，內臣所犯，宜下法司，明正其罪，不當廢祖宗法。」

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Lin Jun said: "Palace and state are one body; offenses by inner eunuchs should go to the judicial offices to clarify their crimes properly — the ancestral law should not be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Lin Jun said, "Palace and state are one body. Offenses by inner eunuchs should go to the judicial offices so their crimes may be properly adjudicated—the Founder's law must not be set aside."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 按太祖之制，內官不得識字、預政，備掃除之役而已。

translations.literal: According to the Founder's regulations, inner eunuchs were not to know writing or participate in government; they were kept only for sweeping duties.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Founder's regulations, inner eunuchs were forbidden to learn writing or take part in government; they existed only to perform menial duties.

sentences.zh: 末年焚錦衣刑具，蓋示永不復用。

translations.literal: In his late years he burned the Embroidered Guard's penal implements — showing they should never be used again.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years he burned the Embroidered Guard's torture implements—a sign that they should never be used again.

sentences.zh: 而成祖違之，卒貽子孫之患，君子惜焉。

translations.literal: Yet Chengzu violated this and ultimately bequeathed calamity to his descendants — men of discernment lament it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chengzu violated this precedent and ultimately bequeathed calamity to his descendants—men of discernment can only lament the result.
